en: The Sūtra of the King of the Most Secret Great Teachings on the Three Vajra Activities of All Tathāgatas, Spoken by the Buddha. Fascicle One.
Translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Imperially Appointed Grand Officer of the Court of State Ceremonial and Acting Director of the Court of State Ceremonial.

Translated by the Dharma-transmitting Master, Your Servant Śīladharma, by Imperial Decree. Chapter One: The Great Maṇḍala of the Samādhi Abiding in All Tathāgatas. The Great Assembly of All Buddhas, the Most Supreme and Profound Secret within Secrets of the Three Vajra Actions of All Tathāgatas. Thus have I heard:

At one time the Buddha was dwelling in the pure realm of manifestations born from the correct wisdom of all Tathāgatas, the vajra actions of the three [body, speech, and mind] of all Tathāgatas, empowered by the supernatural faculties of all Tathāgatas. He was accompanied by an assembly of great bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in as many Mount Sumerus as there are in incalculable and immeasurable buddha-fields. Their names were as follows:

The Bodhisattva Vajrasamādhi, the Bodhisattva Vajrakāya, the Bodhisattva Vajravāk, the Bodhisattva Vajracitta, the Bodhisattva Vajrasamāpatti, the Bodhisattva Vajrāgra, the Bodhisattva Vajrabhūmi, the Bodhisattva Vajrāmbu, the Bodhisattva Vajratejas, the Bodhisattva Vajramarut, the Bodhisattva Vajrākāśa, the Bodhisattva Vajrarūpa, the Bodhisattva Vajraśabda, the Bodhisattva Vajragandha, the Bodhisattva Vajrarasa, the Bodhisattva Vajraspraṣṭavya, the Bodhisattva Vajradharmadhātusvabhāva... these and other such Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas served as the leaders.

At that time, there were all the Tathāgatas equal in number to the realm of empty space—namely, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana-vajra, the Tathāgata Akṣobhya-vajra, the Tathāgata Ratnasambhava-vajra, the Tathāgata Amitāyus-vajra, and the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi-vajra—and all such Tathāgatas as these, pervading empty space like sesame seeds without any intervening gaps, each appearing individually within the void.

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, entered within the great assembly the samādhi of the supreme sovereign great teaching of all Tathāgatas. This samādhi enters from the adorned bodies of all Tathāgatas; while within this samādhi, he completely gathers the body, speech, and mind activities of all Tathāgatas as their great sovereign. In accordance with all sought-after meanings, he manifests various images within a single body and performs various transformations, yet again manifests the original body of Vairocana Buddha, and from within that body, he emerges from samādhi.

Through these transformations, there immediately appeared the Bodhisattva Buddhalocanā, the Bodhisattva Māmakī, the Bodhisattva Pāṇḍaravāsinī, the Bodhisattva Tārā, and so forth; such Bodhisattvas were born and remained.

Furthermore, there appeared the Bodhisattva Rūpasvabhāva, the Bodhisattva Śabdasvabhāva, the Bodhisattva Gandhasvabhāva, the Bodhisattva Rasasvabhāva, the Bodhisattva Sparśasvabhāva, and so forth; such Bodhisattvas were born and remained.

At that time, the World-Honored One, Akṣobhya-vajra Tathāgata, through the power of his sustaining vow, dwelt in accordance with reality within the vast, perfect, and great *samaya* maṇḍala of the pure realm of all Tathāgatas, which pervades the ten directions. Having realized the various forms and images through the contemplation of their intrinsic nature, he brought forth clouds of infinite emanated Buddhas that completely filled the four quarters without any intervening gaps. Within this, the vast and magnificent maṇḍala of the central deity appeared, abiding before all the Buddhas.
Having thus appeared, he dwells in accordance with reality within the great maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas, amidst the three vajra-activities of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One Vairocana-vajra Tathāgata, Akṣobhya-vajra Tathāgata, Ratnasambhava-vajra Tathāgata, Amitāyus-vajra Tathāgata, and Amoghasiddhi-vajra Tathāgata—all these Tathāgatas were fully established in the vajra-bodhicitta.
Having established himself in the bodhicitta, he immediately entered the vajra-samādhi in which all Tathāgatas are manifest and present.

Furthermore, abiding upon the auspicious, pure, great vajra-ground of all Tathāgatas, he caused all sentient beings throughout the entirety of the realm of space to be empowered by Vajrasattva, and they further attained the supreme, wondrous bliss of all Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One, Vairocana-vajra Tathāgata, having emerged from the samādhi born of the three vajra-activities of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, immediately manifested as a Great Vidyādhara who has attained the empowerment of the great vidyās of all Tathāgatas and dwells therein. Extending even to the universal and boundless, he empowered this Vidyādhara; emerging from the bodhicitta of the Buddha World-Honored One, his three faces appeared before all Buddhas, at which time each and every Tathāgata manifested.
At that time, the World-Honored One Akṣobhyavajra Tathāgata and all other Tathāgatas, having emerged from the samādhi of the heart of the Great Vairocana-vajra Tathāgata, each spoke these words:
“Great indeed are all Buddhas, who have all turned their minds toward enlightenment (bodhicitta).
They dwell securely in all Tathāgatas, the secret, supreme, and unimpeded.”
Furthermore, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vairocana-Vajra, snapped his fingers to summon all the Tathāgatas.

At that moment, all the Tathāgatas immediately manifested the Samādhi of Reality and transformed themselves into clouds of jewels, raining down precious offerings to worship the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vairocana-Vajra.
Having made this offering, they prostrated with reverence and all spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!
We all desire to proclaim, according to our own capacities, the adamantine, exquisite, and true Dharma-gate of the Secret Assembly of All Tathāgatas."
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vairocana-Vajra, praised these words:
"Excellent, excellent!

All the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have skillfully performed and skillfully taught this most rare [teaching]. All the bodhisattvas have attained what they never had before, as they have all come to fully comprehend this vast Dharma-gate of the secret reality, severing all doubts; such merit is supreme and peerless."

All the assemblies of all Tathāgatas; the secret three activities of the vajra body, speech, and mind of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas; all that is performed through the empowerment of all Tathāgatas; the authentic words arising from the vajra-samādhi of all Tathāgatas; the supreme ultimate meaning of the most exquisite bliss of all Tathāgatas—and indeed all dharmas such as the wisdom-manifesting wisdom, cause, and effect of all Tathāgatas—may you proclaim them as you see fit; now is the very time for this.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhyavajra, having accepted the exhortation, immediately entered the samādhi of the Great Wisdom Light of All Tathāgatas, the Akṣobhyavajra.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he abided in the three vajra-activities and proclaimed the supreme, most exquisite, essential root-heart *mahāvidyā* of the Vajra Family, saying:

"Oṃ vajratricuḥ. When this *mahāvidyā* was spoken, that Blessed One manifested as a *vidyādhara* emerging from the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, appearing with the three colors of black, white, and red. He was in union with the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) of Akṣobhya Tathāgata and remained established in the supreme, fundamental vajra-activities of all Tathāgatas.
This vidyādhara sits in the eastern direction; he is named the Lord of the Vajra Family.
Furthermore, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhavavajra, entered the samādhi called the Auspicious Vajra of the Jewel-Born of All Tathāgatas.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he proclaimed with his own three karmas the supreme, most exquisite root-heart *mahāvidyā* of the Ratnakula: "Oṃ ratna-triku.

When this *mahāvidyā* was spoken, that Blessed One appeared as a *vidyādhara* from the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, manifesting in the three colors of yellow, white, and black. He entered the realm of space in union with the great mudrā of Ratnasaṃbhava and dwelt within the realm of space, abiding in the vajra-body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
This vidyādhara sits in the south; he is named the Lord of the Ratna Family.
Furthermore, the Bhagavān Vajratathāgata Amitāyus entered the vajra-samādhi called "The Emergence of the Great Lotus Teachings."
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he proclaimed with his own three karmas the supreme, most exquisite root-heart *mahāvidyā* of the Lotus Family, saying:

"Oṃ āḥ hrīḥ. When this *mahāvidyā* was spoken, that Blessed One manifested as a *vidyādhara* arising from the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas; appearing in the three colors of red, white, and black, he was joined with the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) of the Lord of *Mahāvidyās*, Avalokiteśvara, and abided in the supreme vajra-trikāya of all Tathāgatas.
This vidyādhara sits in the western direction; he is named the Lord of the Lotus Family.
Furthermore, the Bhagavān Vajratathāgata Amoghasiddhi entered the vajra-samādhi called the "Vajra Samādhi of the Non-empty Samaya of All Tathāgatas."
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he proclaimed with his own three karmas the supreme and most exquisite root-heart *mahāvidyā* of the *samaya-mantra* of the *Ākarṣaṇa-kula*, saying:

"Oṃ prajñātri kuṃ. When this *mahāvidyā* was spoken, that Blessed One appeared as a *vidyādhara* from the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, manifesting in the three colors of white, black, and green; he was joined with the great seal (*mahāmudrā*) of Amoghasiddhi and abided in the vajra-trikāya of all Tathāgatas.
This vidyādhara sits in the northern direction; he is named the Lord of the Samaya Family.
Furthermore, the Blessed One, Vairocana-vajra Tathāgata, entered the vajra-samādhi called "The Arising of the Samādhi of All Tathāgatas."
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he proclaimed with his own three karmas the supreme, most exquisite root-heart *mahāvidyā* of the Buddha Family, saying:

"Oṃ jina-jikū. When this *mahāvidyā* was spoken, the Vidyādhara appeared from the body, speech, and mind of all those Tathāgatas; manifesting the three colors of black, white, and red, he was in union with the Great Seal (*mahāmudrā*) of Mahāvairocana and abided in the supreme root vajra-trikāya of all the Tathāgatas.
This vidyādhara sits in the center and is called the Lord of the Buddha Family.

Thus, these five families—the Vajra family, the Ratna family, the Padma family, the Samaya family, and the Buddha family—constitute the profound and secret dharma-gates, which are the fivefold secret accomplishments of liberation.
At that time, the World-Honored One, Akṣobhya-vajra Tathāgata, again entered the samādhi of the Vajra Subjugation of the Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he proclaimed from his own body, speech, and mind the root heart-mantra of all the foremost vidyā-consorts within all the Vajra families, saying:

"Oṃ nuviśarati. While this mantra was being spoken, the Vidyādhara Bodhisattva emerged from the body, speech, and mind of all those Tathāgatas; appearing in the form of a woman, he sat in the southeastern corner.
Furthermore, the World-Honored One, Vairocana-Vajra-Tathāgata, entered the *samādhi* called “Vajra Subjugation of All Tathāgatas.
Emerging from that meditative absorption, he proclaimed from his own three karmas the root heart-mantra of all the foremost vidyārājñīs within the family of all Tathāgatas, saying:

“Oṃ muhara-te. When this mantra was spoken, the Vidyādhara Bodhisattva emerged from the body, speech, and mind of all those Buddha-World-Honored Ones; appearing in the form of a woman, he sat in the southwestern corner.
Furthermore, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vajra Amitāyus, entered the *samādhi* called "The Vajra of Subduing through Holding the Lotus of All Tathāgatas.
Emerging from that concentration, he proclaimed with his own three karmas the root heart-mantra of all the foremost vidyārājñīs within the Lotus Family of all Tathāgatas:

"Oṃ āḥ rāgarati. When this mantra was spoken, the vidyādhara bodhisattvas emerged from the body, speech, and mind of that Buddha-World-Honored One; appearing in the form of women, they sat in the northwest corner.
Furthermore, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi-vajra, entered the vajra-samādhi of the speech-trance of all Tathāgatas.
Emerging from that concentration, he proclaimed with his own three karmas the root-heart mahāvidyā-mantra of the foremost vidyārājñīs within the *samaya-ākarṣaṇa-kula* of all Tathāgatas, saying:

"Oṃ vajrarati. When this mahāvidyā-mantra was spoken, the Vidyādhara Bodhisattva emerged from the body, speech, and mind of all those Tathāgatas; appearing in the form of a woman, she sat in the northeastern corner.
Each of these four vidyādhara bodhisattvas is born from the samaya-wisdom of the consort of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again entered the samādhi of the All-Illuminating Vajra.

Having emerged from meditative absorption, he proclaimed with his own three karmas the root-heart mahāvidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Yamāntaka, who abides within the great maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas:

"Oṃ yamāntakṛt huṃ. When this mahāvidyā was spoken, that Blessed One, the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja, emerged from the root of the vidyās of all Tathāgatas—the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas—and sat at the eastern gate.
He again entered the *vajra-samādhi* of the manifest enlightenment of all Tathāgatas.

Emerging from that concentration, he proclaimed with his own three activities the root-heart great mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Prajñāntaka, who abides within the great maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas:

"Oṃ prajñāntakṛt phaṭ. When this great mantra was spoken, that Blessed One emerged from the root of the great mantra of the *vajra-samaya* of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas as the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja and sat at the southern gate.
He again entered the samādhi called "The Act of the Dharma-Jewel of All Tathāgatas.

Emerging from that concentration, he proclaimed with his own three karmas the root-heart mahāvidyā-mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Paṭmaṇḍadeva, who dwells within the great maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas:

"Oṃ paṭmaṇḍade kṛt svāhā. When this vidyā-mantra was spoken, that Blessed One appeared from the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas as the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja, manifesting through the vocal activity of all Tathāgatas, and sat at the western gate.
He again entered the vajra-samādhi of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

Emerging from that meditative absorption, he proclaimed with his own three karmas the root heart-mantra of the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja Vajravināyaka, who abides within the maṇḍala of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas:

"Oṃ vināyake hūṃ tr̥ṭ. When this mantra was spoken, that Blessed One emerged as the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja from the union of the three activities of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas and sat at the northern gate.
Thus, all these great wrathful vidyārājas each dwelt within the great maṇḍala of the great samaya of the great joy of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.

2. The Section on Bodhicitta from the Supreme, Profoundly Secret Assembly of All Tathāgatas’ Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind: The Second Section on Bodhicitta. At that time, all the Tathāgatas performed a great offering with their vajra body, speech, and mind, making offerings to the Tathāgata Vairocana.
Having made these offerings, they each spoke this verse:
"I shall each joyfully proclaim the sublime and wondrous Dharma, The supreme Vajra body, speech, and mind,
And the unsurpassed Great Bodhi, The secret meaning of all Tathāgatas."
At that time, Vairocana-vajra-tathāgata—the Great Secret Lord of the Three Vajra Actions—having heard these verses spoken by all the Tathāgatas, remained silent.
At that time, there were various bodhisattvas in the assembly, each of whom inwardly contemplated this sign with their minds.
Knowing this, the World-Honored One spoke these words within the great assembly:
"O sons of good family!
Whether it be body or mind, the arising of any characteristic is itself the characteristic of abiding.
Since body and mind are free from characteristics, where could they abide?
The same applies to linguistic discrimination.

At that time, having heard this Dharma, all the bodhisattvas became firmly established in the three karmas of all Tathāgatas, free from all marks like space. They gave rise to great joy and spoke these words:
“Great is Samantabhadra, the Great Dharmadhātu! Firm and immovable are body, speech, and mind;
The name ‘born’ corresponds to the unborn— All phenomena of birth are thus.”
At that time, all the Tathāgatas, each having established themselves in the firmness of the three karmas, immediately entered the *vajra-samādhi* of the manifest awakening of all Tathāgatas.
Having emerged from samādhi, they all spoke these words:
"One should know that the bodhicitta is without intrinsic nature (*niḥsvabhāva*).
Nature is not non-nature, and nature is also not nature; if one realizes this nature, one realizes the absence of nature."
One who understands in this way is able to fully realize that unsurpassed nature.
Because of that realization, there is nothing to be attained; this is what is called the firm abiding of all Tathāgatas in the activities of body, speech, and mind.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vairocana-Vajra, entered the Samādhi of the Manifestation of All Tathāgatas’ Vajra.
Emerging from that meditative absorption, he spoke these words:
“You should know:”
The bodhicitta is free from all natures—whether aggregates, bases, or elements—and is without grasping or abandoning.
All phenomena are selfless and arise in equality, yet that mental dharma is fundamentally unborn from the very beginning.
Therefore, one should know that the self-nature of my Dharma is itself emptiness.
One who realizes this is said to be firmly established in the bodhicitta.
Furthermore, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Akṣobhyavajra, immediately entered the *samādhi* of the Inexhaustible Vajra of All Tathāgatas.
Emerging from that concentration, he spoke these words:
"The bodhicitta is without phenomena and without the nature of phenomena; it is unborn and without self. This nature is like space, free from all conceptual characteristics."
"One who understands in this way is said to be firmly established in the bodhicitta.
Furthermore, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhavavajra, entered the samādhi of the Vajra of the Selflessness of Phenomena (dharmanairātmya) of all Tathāgatas.
Having emerged from meditative concentration, he spoke these words:
"The bodhicitta is the absence of intrinsic nature in all phenomena; it is free from the characteristics of all phenomena, and it arises from the reality-limit of the selflessness of phenomena."
"One who understands in this way is said to be firmly established in the bodhicitta.
Furthermore, the World-Honored One, Vairocana-Vajra-Tathāgata, immediately entered the *samādhi* of the Blazing Radiant Light Vajra of All Tathāgatas.
Having emerged from meditative concentration, he spoke these words:

"The bodhicitta is the dharma of non-arising; it is neither with nature nor without nature. It abides in accordance with the phrase 'like space,' and one should practice in this same manner toward all dharmas."
"One who understands in this way is said to be firmly established in the bodhicitta.
Furthermore, the World-Honored One, Vajra Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi, immediately entered the vajra-samādhi called "Abiding in the Presence of All Tathāgatas."
Having emerged from meditative concentration, he spoke these words:

"The bodhicitta is the dharma of intrinsic purity and luminosity; it is not that bodhi possesses any characteristics to be apprehended, nor is it something to be realized through a samādhi manifest before one."
"One who understands in this way is said to be firmly established in the bodhicitta.

At that time, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Maitreya, who, hearing within the great assembly how each of the Tathāgatas had proclaimed the secret dharmatā-mantras through their respective three karmas and taught the dharma of the bodhicitta, gave rise to great joy and marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence. He then spoke these words amidst the assembly:
"How great are all the Buddhas!"
How great is the secret Dharma!
You proclaim the gateway to the sublime Dharma, the meaning of ultimate purity, and the teaching on the bodhicitta; to you I pay homage and offer praise.
Born from selflessness, all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas have already transcended all doubts; signless and unimpeded,
they all abide in the bodhicitta— to them I pay homage and offer praise.
The universal meaning of Samantabhadra arises from the bodhicitta;
likewise, all those practices arise from the conduct of awakening.
To this firm bodhicitta, I pay homage and offer praise.
The Tathāgata’s mind is pure; this is the bodhicitta.
His physical and verbal activities are firm, known as the three vajra-activities.
To the Buddha’s awakening, the ultimate refuge, I pay homage and offer praise.

3. The Section on the Vajra-Adornment Samādhi. From the *Vajra-Adornment Samādhi*, the third section of the *Great Assembly of All Buddhas* within the most profound secret among secrets of the supreme vajra-body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas. At that time, the Bhagavān Mahāvairocana Vajra-Tathāgata again entered the *Vajra-Samādhi Adorned by the Great Cloud of Emanations of All Tathāgatas*.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he then uttered this great mantra:
"Oṃ śuddhasvabhāvātmako haṃ. Having spoken this great mantra, he further spoke these verses:
"Within the expanse of space, Visualize the Buddha-maṇḍala."
The Great Array of Clouds of Radiance, the Buddha’s Equal Flame-Light;
The five kinds of equal light form the equal circular mandala.
The liberation from the nature of the five desires is called the practice of the five masteries.
Abiding in the visualization of equanimity, within the image of the Buddha,
one dwells in the union of the three activities through the Great Seal (Mahāmudrā) of the Universal Illuminator (Samantabhadra).
With vajra body, speech, and mind, one abides in the visualization of the Great Seal.
The great seal of the Honored One Akṣobhya gives rise to the corresponding practices;
The great seal of the Honored One Ratnasambhava; The wisdom-light of Amitāyus;
The seal of Amoghasiddhi— Visualize these as the Buddha maṇḍala.
He manifests the great light of sapphire blue, abiding in the steadfastness of the three karmas;
he holds the great flame of the vajra, with a most fierce and terrifying appearance.
He manifests the moonlight of crystal, adorning his topknot and crown.
Holding a blazing great wheel, adorned with all purities;
manifesting light of purple-gold hue, Buddha-clouds illuminate all quarters;
visualizing oneself holding a nine-pronged vajra.
Manifesting coral-colored light, adorned with adamantine flames,
holding the radiance of great jewels, and pervaded by blazing clouds;
manifesting lotus-colored light, adorning the topknot crown.
Holding a blazing lotus, visualize it as the Lotus-Vajra.
These five kinds of light are the mark of the unerring and firm;
skillfully wielding the sword of wisdom, visualize the Buddha-maṇḍala.
Having spoken these verses, he again entered the samādhi of the intrinsic nature of the dharma-realm of all Tathāgatas.

Emerging from that concentration, he further spoke the great vidyā-mantra for the empowerment of the three vajra-actions: “Oṃ dharmadhātu-vajra svabhāvātmako ’ham. Having spoken this vidyā-mantra, he further spoke these verses:
"The five kinds of great jewels appear, each the size of a mustard seed;
peerless and most supreme, they abide eternally in meditative equipoise.
These jewels dwell in vastness, yet their non-abiding is likewise vast."
That vast cloud of jewels is the Buddha’s impartial radiance.
Manifesting the great vajra-wheel, it brings forth a great cloud of jewels;
holding the treasury of the great lotus, it grasps the implements of its own family.
Furthermore, clouds of bodhisattvas appear, vast and without limit;
they manifest sovereign transformations, all of them unimpeded.
Within the realm of empty space, they manifest the moon maṇḍala.
From the maṇḍala and so forth, one should visualize the perfection of the great wheel.
One should visualize the lotus maṇḍala as having the nature of vajra;
from the jewel maṇḍala arises the jewel of naturally pure essence.
The corresponding maṇḍala arises from the characteristic of space;
it is the supreme nature of the Buddha, the accomplishment of body, speech, and mind.
This firm arising possesses the characteristics of omniscience.
At that time, the Buddha, the World-Honored One, Mahāvairocana,
again snapped his fingers to summon all the Tathāgatas.
Thereupon, all those Tathāgatas once more gathered like clouds.
He exhorted the Honored Vairocana to teach the maṇḍala rite:
“The tranquility of all Tathāgatas, The source of all Tathāgatas,
The supreme dharma of selflessness— I pray that you will teach the maṇḍala.”
Perfectly complete in all aspects, adorned with every mark,
the supreme body of Samantabhadra— may you proclaim the maṇḍala.
Born from the tranquil Dharma, purified by the practice of right wisdom.
O Samantabhadra of supreme speech, please explain the maṇḍala.
The great mind of all sentient beings is by nature pure and stainless;
O Samantabhadra of supreme mind, please explain the maṇḍala.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the most supreme honored one of the three realms,
the savior of the three realms, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva [said]:
“The great mind of all Tathāgatas, the source from which all Tathāgatas arise...”
The nature of all maṇḍalas is now proclaimed in sequence.
I shall now explain the supreme Great Mind Maṇḍala,
which abides as the Vajra of Mind and the maṇḍala of the three activities.
With the mind of faith and resolve as the thread, one performs the work according to the prescribed proportions;
measuring with wisdom, one dwells in the visualization of the three karmas.
One should construct the great-citta maṇḍala to the measure of twelve cubits.
In the four cardinal directions and the four intermediate corners, with four gates and four pavilions,
place a great wheel at the center, complete and without deficiency;
each [deity] abides in its respective mudrā, performing the rites according to the ritual manual.
Within the wheel, one should visualize a vajra, manifesting as a great light of indranīla-blue;
it is a five-pronged wisdom-vajra with a terrifying appearance of blazing flames.
In the east, one should visualize a great wheel, adorned with vajra-light.
In the south, one should visualize a great jewel, manifesting the radiance of various gems;
in the west, a great lotus, manifesting light the color of a lotus;
in the north, a great sharp sword, emitting blazing light.
In the southeast corner is Locanā, manifesting light the color of blue clouds;
in the southwest corner is the Wisdom-Vajra, from which Māmakī is born;
in the northwest corner is the Lotus, appearing in its full-blown form.
In the northeast corner is a blue lotus, with the pure light of the color of blue clouds.
Next, at the eastern gate, one should visualize Maṇikula;
at the southern gate, visualize the jewel-staff, with the pure radiance of vajra-flames.
Visualize a lotus at the western gate, manifesting blazing sword-rays;
at the northern gate, a vajra, a vajra-vase, and so forth.
Having visualized in this manner, the mind-maṇḍala is perfected.
Through the three vajra activities, perform vast offerings.
If one abides in the offering of the body, there is no obstruction regarding bodily forms;
if one abides in the offering of the mind, one realizes the equality of the nature of mind.
The wise one dwells securely, possessing immeasurable merit;
through these auspicious verses of the Buddhas, the realm of space is adorned.
If one makes worldly offerings—such as incense, flowers, lamps, and ointments—
They shall attain the joy of the noble ones and be revered by all Bodhisattvas. Chapter Five:

The Practice of All Illuminating Phrases The Supreme Assembly of All Buddhas within the Most Profound Secret among Secrets of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas At that time, the World-Honored One, the Great Vairocana Vajra-Tathāgata—the Great Sovereign of the Three Vajra Actions, the Great Vajradhara King, the most supreme and autonomous one in all places, who skillfully expounds the meaning and characteristics of all practices of all dharmas—spoke these words to the great assembly:
“O Great Beings, you should know:”
All those phenomena are free from doubt and arise as reality.
Whether it be desire, hatred, or delusion—these three are equal.
To realize this nature of phenomena is itself the nature of unsurpassed, great Bodhi.
Having understood this, one attains all accomplishments.

Even if there are those among the world’s outcastes (*caṇḍāla*) or other evil classes who constantly harbor intentions to kill and harm sentient beings, if they can practice the secret [teachings] with pure faith and understanding, such persons will all attain accomplishment and be able to dwell securely in the Mahāyāna secret.

"Furthermore, if there are sentient beings who have committed the deeds of immediate retribution and have extensively perpetrated various evils and most grievous sins, yet are able to give rise to pure faith and practice the secret [mantras], they too shall attain all supreme accomplishments."

If there are sentient beings who have committed the karma of killing, practiced taking what is not given, engaged in various forms of sexual misconduct, or uttered great falsehoods—and those who have created such evil karmas—if they can give rise to pure faith and understanding and practice the secret dharma, even such persons will attain accomplishment.
Why is this? Great beings,
you should know that within the secret Dharma, whether it be defilement or purity, whether it be enmity or intimacy, all are entirely equal.
If one understands this, one will be able to abide in the most supreme secret essentials of the Mahāyāna; this is the accomplishment of the self-nature of all Buddhas.

For this reason, one attains freedom from doubt regarding all phenomena, with the sole exception of those who slander the ācārya; such persons, even if they diligently seek the secret dharma, will not achieve accomplishment.

At that time, there was in the assembly a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin. Having heard the Buddha, the World-Honored One, preach this Dharma, he marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."
"How is it that you proclaim this meaning before the Tathāgatas and the great assembly—a meaning I have never heard before?
Is this the teaching of the Dharma or of what is not the Dharma?
I pray that the Buddha, the World-Honored One, will explain this to me."
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed the Bodhisattva Sarvanīvaraṇaviṣkambhin, saying:
"Stop, stop, son of good family!"
Do not speak thus.

You should know that what is spoken is the very nature of all phenomena, the true pure wisdom of all Tathāgatas, and the source from which the subtle and supreme ultimate meaning of all phenomena arises; this is called the phrase for the practice of bodhi.

Furthermore, within the assembly, there were all those bodhisattvas—numbering as many as the atoms in Mount Sumeru in all the countless and immeasurable Buddha-fields—who, upon hearing the Buddha preach this Dharma, were all struck with great terror and alarm; they fainted and fell to the ground, each thinking:
"We pray only that the World-Honored One will bestow compassion and protection, so that we may return to our original seats."

At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vairocana-Vajra, knowing their thoughts, immediately entered the *vajrasamādhi* of the non-dual equality of space and the three vajra-actions of all Tathāgatas. Within that meditative absorption, through the empowerment of the supernatural power of the three vajra-actions, the assembly of Bodhisattvas was instantly awakened; freed from all fears, they were each able to return to their respective seats.

At that time, all the Tathāgatas, having witnessed this event, were filled with great joy and gave rise to a sense of wonder; they all spoke these verses in pure, profound, and wondrous Dharma-sounds:
"How magnificent is the supreme Dharma!
How great is the one born from the meaning of the Dharma!
To the true selflessness of phenomena, I pay homage to the Vajra King.
With body, speech, and mind purified, he abides in the equality of space.
Free from doubt and unimpeded, I take refuge in the Vajra Body.
The Tathāgata’s mind is supreme; it follows the path of the three periods of time.
The realm of True Suchness is free from characteristics; I take refuge in that which is like space.
The body of space is the reality; The speech of space is well-turned;
The dharmas of space are pure— I take refuge in that which is beyond analogy. Chapter Six:

The Empowerment of Body, Speech, and Mind This is the sixth chapter, the Empowerment of Body, Speech, and Mind, from the Great Assembly of All Buddhas, the Most Supreme and Profound Secret within Secrets of the Vajra Three Actions of All Tathāgatas. At that time, the Blessed One, Akṣobhya Vajra Tathāgata, again entered the samādhi of the secret body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he proclaimed the heart-mantra of empowerment, saying:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatādhipativajra svabhāvātmako ’ham. Furthermore, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vairocana-vajra, having emerged from that absorption, again entered the *viraja-vajra-samādhi*.
Having emerged from this, he proclaimed the *vidyā* for the empowerment of the body, saying:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatākāyavajra svabhāvādya kuṅkham. Furthermore, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Vajra Amitāyus, entered the *samādhi* of the Non-dual Equality Vajra.
Emerging from meditative absorption, he proclaimed the mantra of empowered speech:

"Oṃ sarvatathāgatavajra svabhāvātmako ’ham. These three vajras are the great secret syllables of all the Tathāgatas; they are free from all conceptualization and discrimination, and abide as the aspect of all mantra practices.
Furthermore, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Ratnasaṃbhava-vajra, entered the *jñānapradīpa-vajra-samādhi*.
Emerging from that meditative absorption, he uttered this great mantra:
"Oṃ sarvatathāgatānurāgaṇavajra svabhāvātmako ’ham. Furthermore, the Blessed One, the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi-vajra, entered the *amoghavajra-samādhi*.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he spoke this great mantra for making offerings to all Buddhas:

"Oṃ sarvatathāgatapūjāvajra svabhāvātmako ’ham. With this great mantra, one should make offerings to all Buddhas by means of the five kinds of unimpeded qualities and the five kinds of practices. Having made such offerings, one swiftly attains the accomplishment of the self-nature of all Buddhas; one is then able to abide in the vajra-body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, and is thus a Vajradhara.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Vajradhara, having rejoiced in all the Tathāgatas’ respective utterances of the great mantras, likewise personally abided in the gateway of mantra practice (*vidyā-caryā-mukha*). He remained entirely tranquil in the three karmas of his own body, speech, and mind; he clearly realized the vast gateway of the methods of accomplishment (*siddhi-dharma-mukha*);
his mind dwelt in selflessness, giving rise to great joy, while his two karmas of body and speech were free from all signs of existence.
Thus, these three types of action are in accord with one another, like space, abiding in equanimity.

One thoroughly realizes that the intrinsic nature of the actions of body, speech, and mind is entirely unapprehendable; by this, one attains correspondence with the intrinsic nature of the characteristics of mantra practice (*mantracaryā*), which is not an object of intellectual cognition nor an object of mental observation, and is far removed from the fabrications of all conditioned activities.
And since those aspects of body, speech, and mind are in correspondence with the self-nature of that bodhi, he thus proclaimed the ritual manual for the great mantra (mahāvidyā).
At that time, the Venerable Vajrapāṇi, abiding in the radiance of all Buddhas and the omniscience of all Buddhas, spoke this supreme visualization:
"Abiding in the midst of space, one should visualize the moon maṇḍala,
manifesting the images of all Buddhas, in accordance with the subtle practices.
One should contemplate in this way:"
“Oṃ. One should abide in single-minded concentration, visualizing mustard seeds filling the void,
and contemplating the syllables of all-encompassing wisdom— the secret ritual of gnosis.”
Furthermore, abiding in the midst of space, one should visualize a sun maṇḍala manifesting the images of all Buddhas, with every syllable complete.
One should contemplate in this way:
“The syllable HŪṂ.

Again, dwelling in the midst of space, one should visualize a precious maṇḍala appearing with various jewel-like forms; contemplate it as perfectly complete.
Again, dwelling in the contemplation of space, one should visualize a lotus maṇḍala.
In union with the vajra-mark, visualize the lotus-vajra.
Abiding further in the contemplation of emptiness, visualize the maṇḍala of light,
wherein the auspicious marks of all Buddhas appear, surrounded by supreme radiance.
Again, visualize the form of a blue lotus and a five-pronged vajra, with various jewels the size of barley grains; fix the mind and perform this visualization.
Again, visualize an eight-petaled lotus, the size of a *lañcana*.
Having stabilized the mind through visualization, one dedicates [the merit] toward Great Enlightenment.
The wheels and so forth are all most supreme; visualizing according to the ritual manual, one accomplishes the syllables of enlightenment and perfects all merits.
The Great Illumination is the most supreme practice;
abiding securely in the Buddha’s Bodhi, it gives birth to all dharmic phrases and dwells within the three vajra actions.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, for the benefit of all sentient beings, [spoke thus].
He taught these pure practices, the most supreme among secrets:
"Within the limits of phenomena, remaining unattached while dwelling amidst the defilements of the dust,
to perform secret offerings— this is called the 'Mental Offering'."
If one partakes of the food of ambrosia, one will attain the fruit of the ultimate meaning,
the supreme and true Dharma, the bodhicitta free from signs.
One should always eat according to the Dharma by means of these four kinds of food.
Abiding in the secrets of the three karmas, all things will be accomplished.
Although one may constantly consume these four, do not give rise to thoughts of obstruction;
remaining free from these four unrighteous acts, one should realize the true nature of food and drink.
One shall obtain the respect and affection of all Buddhas,
as well as the wisdom of Bodhisattvas and their various corresponding practices, swiftly accomplishing the Buddha-nature.
One shall attain mastery within the realm of desire, as well as success in all undertakings.
Attaining majestic radiance, physical beauty, and strength, all will revere and love them.
Possessing great renown throughout the world, those who behold them are as if illuminated by light;
this is the secret of all Buddhas and the supreme state of all Bodhisattvas.
"This is called the True Dharma Gate of the Vajra Three Karmas of All Secret Great Illumination Practices.
Thus spoke the Buddha in the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra*, the Supreme Secret Great King of Teachings on the Vajra Three Karmas of All Tathāgatas, Volume One.
Thus spoke the Buddha in the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra*, the Supreme Secret [of the Vajra Three Karmas of All Tathāgatas]...

The Section on the Secret and Sublime Conduct. The Seventh Section on the Secret and Sublime Conduct from the Great Assembly of All Buddhas within the Most Supreme and Profound Secret among Secrets of the Vajra Three Karmas of All Tathāgatas. At that time, the World-Honored One, the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again proclaimed the Samādhi Dharma of the Supreme and True Great Mantra of the Great Samaya of the Vajra Three Karmas of All Tathāgatas, in verse:
"Whatever wealth and pleasures one delights in, may they be practiced according to one's wish;
obtaining various corresponding attainments, may one swiftly accomplish the Buddha-nature.
Furthermore, whatever wealth and pleasures one delights in, may they be practiced according to one's wish."
Having attained union with the *iṣṭadevatā*, one accomplishes the offerings for oneself and others.
Even if one performs ascetic practices to seek the Dharma, they cannot achieve accomplishment;
rather, it is the spontaneous engagement in all pleasures that constitutes true, excellent accomplishment.
Even if one were to seek sustenance by wandering in the four directions for food and drink,
by maintaining the recitation without interruption, one will attain all forms of wealth and happiness.
Abiding well in body, speech, and mind, one should diligently seek great enlightenment.
One will be far removed from the fear of untimely death and shall not fall into hell.
This is the practice of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, the supreme practice of great vidyā;
it consists of the syllables of the sublime Dharma and brings about the accomplishment of all wealth and happiness.
Proceeding through all realms of pleasure, one attains mastery over the five wisdoms;
this is constantly praised by Bodhisattvas and is the virtuous deed of all Buddhas.
One should know that the three kinds of form accomplish the offerings of oneself and others.
The "Beloved by All Buddhas" is born from the Honored One Vairocana;
furthermore, the three kinds of sounds are for making offerings to all the noble sages.
The "Beloved by All Buddhas" is born from the Honored One Ratnaketu.
Furthermore, there are three kinds of incense; by offering them to all Buddhas and others, one gains the affection of all Buddhas and is born into the realm of Amitāyus.
Furthermore, there are three kinds of flavors; by offering them to all the noble sages, [one attains...]
The Veneration of All Buddhas, born from the Honored One Amoghasiddhi;
furthermore, by touching the three types [of objects], one makes offerings to one’s own family.
Those Buddhas of the Vajra [family] are those attained by the Honored One Akṣobhya.
Regarding those forms, sounds, scents, and so forth, the mind should always remain free from all fetters.
All the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have taught this secret truth:
one should contemplate with a focused mind the mantra-syllables of form, sound, and the rest.
Furthermore, within each respective family, visualize all the noble ones;
abiding in correspondence with the mindfulness of the Buddha, perform the visualization of the ritual action.
Contemplating the activities of body, speech, and mind, one accomplishes the visualization of vajra-mindfulness.
Through association with the mindfulness of the various families, one accomplishes the contemplation of wrath;
through association with the mindfulness of the noble ones, one accomplishes the contemplation of awakening.
If one abides in the contemplation of the body, then the bodily marks are without obstruction.
If one dwells with the mind in visualization, the mind becomes free from all attachments.
This is what all Buddhas love and delight in; dwelling in the observation of the Buddha-eye, both places are equal, and one swiftly accomplishes the Buddha-nature.
The ritual procedures for the syllables HŪṂ and OṂ, as well as the syllable PHAṬ and others,
manifest five kinds of light; one should visualize the Lotus-Vajra with the pure radiance of the moon’s flames, contemplating it according to one's will.
In meditative equipoise with the recollection of the Buddha, one contemplates and seeks awakening.
What is the contemplation of the recollection of the Buddha?
It means that throughout all places, there are the images of all Buddhas, from which clouds of Buddha-wisdom emerge.
What is the contemplation of the recollection of phenomena (*dharmānusmṛti*)?
It means pervading all places, visualizing the vajra-dharma, and causing clouds of dharma-wisdom to appear.
What is the vajra-contemplation?
That is to say, pervading all places, one visualizes Vajrasattva, manifesting clouds of vajra-wisdom.
What is the visualization of the various families?
It means pervading all places, manifesting the images of the deities and the clouds of the deities' wisdom.
What is the meditation on wrath?
It means that throughout all places, one should bring to mind the sound of wrath and manifest clouds of wrathful wisdom.
What is the meditation on bodhi, and what is the mindfulness of that bodhi?
That is to say, the original Vajra-lotus, with both places entirely equal, manifests the sun of wisdom-vajra; perform the vajra-offering.
Furthermore, how is it named? It is called the "contemplation of the maṇḍala."
That is to say, the equality of the two places, the sovereign power of the wondrous lotus,
the arising of the great correspondence— the very nature of the maṇḍala.
What is the contemplation of mindfulness of the body?
All supreme and wondrous bodies, with the nature of the five aggregates fully perfected—
the self-nature of those Buddhas' bodies is seen as equal in this way.
What is the contemplation of speech and thought?
That is to say, the Vajra Dharma-speech views all things as equal in this way, upholding the supreme dharmatā.
How does one contemplate with mental recollection?
Pervading all things, one abides in the secret root.
Seeing equality in this way, one maintains the great mind of Vajra.
How does one contemplate sentient beings, as well as their physical and verbal actions? Seeing equality in this way—
All are free from characteristics and equal, Everything is like space.
How, then, can they be named The characteristics of all great luminosities?
It refers to the dharmas of the body, speech, and mind, In which mindfulness and contemplation are in accord.
The body abides as the sublime vajra; speech and mind are likewise so.
To cultivate such an equalizing vision is called the supreme upholding of the sublime.
Furthermore, what is meant by the recollection and contemplation of the samaya?
That is to say, the syllables of samādhi, The pure ritual procedures,
adorned by the Tathāgata, Attain the accomplishment of sublime bliss.
Furthermore, what is the name Of the Prajñāpāramitā?
In the recollection and contemplation of the samaya,
there is pure great radiance; it is unborn and without support,
without wisdom and without attainment, without cause and without that which is produced.
Furthermore, what is called that contemplation on the thought of non-arising?
It is the self-nature of all phenomena, the pure and luminous dharma,
which, like space, is free from characteristics.
Furthermore, it is free from words; neither dual nor non-dual, it is stainless and tranquil.
Moreover, what is the name for the visualization of the offerings to the various families?
That is to say, with body and mind free from signs,
one performs equal offerings in resonance with all the families, thereby accomplishing the nectar-dharma.
One attains the Buddha’s empowered body, as well as that vajra-mind.
The speech of the supreme upholding of the Dharma is all obtained in accordance with reality.
With body, speech, and mind purified, and far removed from all perverse thoughts,
one accomplishes the conduct of a Vidyādhara and attains indestructible vajra-nature.

Chapter Eight: The Amṛta Samādhi Section from the Supreme, Most Profound, Secret of Secrets Great Assembly of All Tathāgatas’ Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind. At that time, the Bhagavān Ratnasaṃbhava-vajra-tathāgata, abiding in the vajra body, speech, and mind of all tathāgatas, addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi—the supreme, sovereign Vajradhara—within the great assembly, praising and exhorting him with these words:
“O Mahāyāna Vajra-being, Abiding in the pure conduct of emptiness, Samantabhadra of the great offerings, Please proclaim the supreme practice.”
The defiled natures of greed, hatred, and delusion, Together enter the Vajrayāna;
equal to space, This is the non-abiding great offering.
The destination of the path of liberation, proclaimed by the three vehicles alike—
the Buddha’s great bliss and purity— please teach the method of making offerings.
With the vastness of the bodhicitta, you skillfully turn the sublime wheel of Dharma.
With body, speech, and mind purified, I take refuge in the Vajrayāna.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi,
having received the Buddha’s exhortation, immediately proclaimed the method of offering:
"Pervading all of empty space, manifesting the vast form of the letter AṂ,
the meaning of all empowerments, it encompasses the Vajra Jewel Family.
Abiding in the three vajras, it is the sublime bliss of body, speech, and mind."
The Dharma from which all Buddhas are born is the offering to all Tathāgatas.
Those who practice this offering abide in the equality of body and mind,
free from attachment and unimpeded.
When the nature of all phenomena is realized throughout the entire expanse of the earth, everything becomes utterly pure.
Devoid of characteristics and profoundly tranquil, there is not the slightest differentiation among phenomena;
all this is the work of the supernatural powers and wisdom of the Tathāgatas.
The secret, most supreme dharma, born from the five families,
should abide in the void; one should visualize the great ocean of wisdom,
with oneself situated within a moon disc, adorned with various ornaments.

One visualizes a stupa, lofty, vast, and exquisitely wondrous, adorned with four jewels,
encircled by a pure garland of five-colored lights.
Again, contemplate the great ocean of wisdom, Which has no abiding mark throughout the three periods of time;
Vast and inconceivable, it universally encompasses all phenomena.
Contemplate that from within one's own pores, Clouds of wisdom for making offerings appear.
And the five kinds of lotuses, namely the blue lotus and so forth;
there are three kinds of flowers that arise from the manifestation of noble sages:
the karnikāra flower, the mallikā flower, and [the others].
The *yūthikā* and *karavīra* flowers,
each one exceptionally sublime, with their exquisite fragrances pervading everywhere;
visualize the wheel maṇḍala, complete with all manner of adornments.
Extending over a vast measure of one hundred yojanas, it is perfectly complete on all sides.
Visualizing with wisdom the vajra, the lotus, the wheel,
the sword, and so forth, each appears within the void.
Extending for many millions of yojanas, pure and adorned on all four sides,
this stūpa composed of various jewels is by nature pure and stainless.
Contemplate it with right wisdom as the cause for making offerings to all the families.
With five kinds of supreme merit, one forms an ocean-like cloud of offerings.
With precious robes pure and stainless, one makes offerings while seeking bodhi;
by performing these five kinds of offerings, one gains the joy of the sages and saints.
Visualize various supreme jewels appearing as adornments;
through all those wondrous gems, one attains the highest accomplishment.
Adorned with the seven treasures, the entire realm becomes perfectly complete.
Abiding in right wisdom, one accomplishes various meanings;
through the supreme form of the Great Seal, within the Buddha-maṇḍala,
one attains union with all tactile sensations and the accomplishment of all flavors.
Abiding in the contemplation of emptiness, one visualizes the maṇḍala adorned with jewels;
one's own essence is the Buddha-body, through which one performs vast offerings.
That supreme secret accords with all phenomena.
Abiding in the phrase of empowerment is the true offering.
All the flavors of nectar can nourish and sustain wisdom;
abiding in the three karmas of all Buddhas, one accomplishes vajra-knowledge.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi further manifested the form of the syllable *Aḥ*,
the practice of all empowerments, and all supreme sovereignty;
through the union of body, speech, and mind, he [manifested] the maṇḍala of the three karmas.
He proclaimed the supreme Dharma, the secret wisdom of all Buddhas:
"One should dwell in the contemplation of emptiness and visualize the Vajra Maṇḍala,
within which the Honored One Akṣobhya appears."
Great flames blaze with intensity, The five kinds of light are perfected;
Born from the Buddhas of the three times, A manifestation of the Vajra family,
In union with body, speech, and mind.
The supreme dharma of meditative concentration, accomplished through a mind of equanimity, is the secret vajra of all; it can destroy everything.
Born from the Vajra of Akṣobhya, it abides in the realm of all Buddhas.
"Thus is called the visualization method for the true samādhi of Akṣobhya Tathāgata within the Vajra Family.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi— accomplished in the liberation of wisdom,
pure by nature and stainless— entered the practice of Great Bodhi."
He taught the Samādhi of Reality, the dharma for attaining the Bodhi of Buddhahood:
"One should abide in the midst of space and visualize the Buddha-maṇḍala,
wherein the Honored One Vairocana appears."
Furthermore, one should visualize all Buddhas in union with their consorts, forming the image of Vajra.
From those three vajras, there emerge all manner of wondrous jewels and impartial wish-fulfilling gems, manifesting as a perfect ocean of jewels.
"The Buddhas, the Great Munis, give birth to the sons of the Buddhas.
Thus is called "The Visualization Method of the Great Wisdom of All Families, the True Samādhi of Vairocana Tathāgata within the Buddha Family."
At that time, Vajrapāṇi spoke on liberation through the nature of passion:
"The secret purity, free from attachment, is the Lotus Maṇḍala."
Abiding in the midst of empty space, one should visualize the great maṇḍala;
within it appears Amitāyus and the offerings to all Buddhas.
This accords with the secret practice, as well as the visualization of all teachings.
This supreme vajra corresponds to the four samādhis.
Through the correspondence of the two roots, it can give birth to the two kinds [of results].
By visualizing all the Tathāgatas, one accomplishes the three vajras.
"Thus, this is called the visualization method for the true samādhi of the Tathāgata Amitāyus within the Lotus Family.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, who has arisen from the wisdom of selflessness and the meaning of the vajra-mantra syllables, proclaimed this teaching:
"Abiding in the midst of space, visualize the maṇḍala of the Buddha,
manifesting Amoghasiddhi and visualizing all the Buddhas.
All Buddhas are non-abiding, free from signs and all verbal expressions."
Reality and delusion, as well as reflections, all abide within the vajra phrase.

firm and indestructible, proclaimed this meaning:
