even if they speak words that are not the Dharma, they shall still attain pure wisdom.
"Thus, this is called the 'Contemplation Method of the Vajra-Wisdom Ornament Samādhi of Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata within the Jewel Family.

At that time, in the assembly, there was a bodhisattva named Vajradhvaja of the Samādhis of All Buddhas, together with incalculable and immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, as numerous as the atoms in Mount Sumeru. Having heard these teachings spoken by all the Tathāgatas, they marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence and immediately raised their voices within the assembly, saying in unison:

'The Great Secret Lord of all Buddha-Tathāgatas transcends the triple world and has penetrated all phenomena of the world; how can it be said herein that speech which is not the Dharma can produce pure wisdom?'"
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vairocana-Vajra, addressed the bodhisattvas,
saying: "Stop,
noble sons!"
Do not speak thus. Why is this?

You should know that those most supreme secret practices are the practices of the bodhisattvas; those practices of the bodhisattvas are the practices of the Tathāgatas; and those practices of the Tathāgatas are the mantra practices.
"O sons of good family!
For example, just as space has no characteristic of dwelling anywhere, and space dwells nowhere, so it is with all phenomena.
Since all phenomena are thus, where could they possibly dwell?"
They do not abide in the desire realm, they do not abide in the form realm, they do not abide in the formless realm, and they do not abide in the four great elements and so forth.
O sons of good family!
All dharmas are without abiding; this meaning is quiescent—thus should you understand it.

The Tathāgatas, knowing the inclinations and desires of all sentient beings, proclaim all Dharma-gates in accordance with them; yet the teachings they deliver are like space, free from all marks of existence, and the samādhi of the Tathāgatas likewise has no abiding place.

“Good sons! It is as if there were a person who, taking a shaft of bamboo, drills wood to produce fire. By applying diligent effort, smoke gradually arises, and before long, fire finally emerges; yet once it has emerged, it immediately goes out. That fire which has been produced does not abide in the bamboo shaft, nor does it abide in the wood, nor does it abide in the person’s hand.”
"O sons of good family!
The samādhis of all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are likewise thus: they abide nowhere, neither coming nor going; all dharmas are also like this."

At that time, when the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas had heard the Buddha, the World-Honored One, teach this Dharma, they gave rise to faith and understanding, marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence, and with great joy, spoke these words of praise:
"Vast, rare, and supreme is this Dharma, Free from marks, quiescent like space;
A pure gateway that tears asunder the net of doubt— Therefore we praise this teaching of truth."

10. The Tenth Chapter: The Examination of the Hearts of All Tathāgatas, from the *Sarvatathāgata-vajra-kāya-vāk-citta-parama-gambhīra-rahasya-rahasya-sarvabuddha-samāja*, entitled "The Examination of the Hearts of All Tathāgatas. At that time, the Blessed One, the Vajra-Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again summoned all the Buddha-Tathāgatas and caused them to universally abide in the secret dharma-gate of the Buddha-Tathāgatas—the firm three karmas of the direct realization of awakening through the Great Samaya-Vajra Reality.
Once they were thus established, Vairocana spoke these words:
"I shall now proclaim the methods for the supreme accomplishment of the secrets of body, speech, and mind—the true vidyās of the various Buddha families."

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi manifested great majestic power within the assembly; his eyes flashed with light, blazing and terrifying. He gazed widely upon the great gathering and the worlds of the ten directions, and emitting a great sound, he spoke these words:
“Vajra body, speech, and mind, Abiding in the visualization of the three activities, Free from doubt and unimpeded, Equanimous and dwelling nowhere.”
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vairocana-Vajra, entered the vajra-samādhi of the instruction on the Perfection of the Tathāgata’s own-nature purity.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he addressed all the Tathāgatas, saying:

"Aksobhya and all other Tathāgatas are each able to proclaim countless koṭis, nayutas, and hundreds of thousands of great mantras that give rise to all accomplishments, manifest various transformations, exercise sovereign supernatural powers throughout the worlds of the ten directions, move in accordance with all dharmas, sport without hindrance among the five sense objects, and are in accord with liberation through the practice of *mantra*."

Why is this? Because from the mantra-practice methods of all Tathāgatas, those great Vidyādharas are born, who are able to contemplate the meaning of the secret great vidyās of the body, speech, and mind of these Tathāgatas; they penetrate and illuminate the heart of all supreme secret great vidyās, and constantly delight in seeking the samādhis of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, constantly delight in seeking the samādhis of the body, speech, and mind of all Vajradharas, and constantly delight in seeking the samādhis of the body, speech, and mind of all Dharma-holders.
Having spoken this Dharma, he then uttered the great mantra (*mahāvidyā*) with his own vajra threefold activity (*trikarma*):
"HŪṂ OṂ ĀḤ SVĀHĀ. When this mantra was spoken, all the bodhisattvas in the assembly were struck with fear upon hearing it, and each of them called to mind the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, knowing this thought, immediately spoke the Great Samādhi Dharma of all Tathāgatas:
"Abiding in the contemplation of emptiness, one should visualize the adorned maṇḍala;
within it, one should visualize the syllable HŪṂ, as well as one’s own image and so forth."
The great radiance of the vajra, vast and inconceivable—
one should contemplate the body, speech, and mind of all Buddhas in this way.
In a single instant, one accomplishes the great vajra of the three activities;
as the Great Being, the Vajrarāja, one attains supreme mastery over all.
Through the self-mantra and the self-mandala ritual, one gives rise to all the various rites.
This summarizes all vidyās, as taught by the Vajra Essence.
One manifests as a self-holding vidyādhara, possessing the physical marks at the four places,
endowed with three faces, and visualizing the three types of colors.
"Thus is called the Dharma of the Space-Vajra Samādhi.
Furthermore, it is said: 'This is the supreme Vajra-secret heart;
one should abide in the contemplation of space and visualize the subtle maṇḍala.'"
Within that, one should further visualize a five-pronged vajra;
maintain this visualization constantly, without allowing for any interruption.
Contemplate the three vajras as well as that vajra hook.
He summons all minds, as well as the various worthies and sages.
He then spoke this great vidyā-mantra:
"All these vajras accomplish the awakening of the Buddhas."
Visualizing the vajra hooks of all the Vajra family, as well as those of the Jewel and Lotus families,
one summons the members of all the families. Then,
contemplating one's own mind, one performs the nāṭaka rite.
Within seven days and nights, perform the vajra activities;
accomplish the body, speech, and mind—the secret wisdom vajra.
Contemplating all aspirations for giving, do not allow fear to arise;
through the vast accomplishment of giving, the mind gives rise to great joy and love,
thereby accomplishing the mantras of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
If one transgresses this dharma, his life shall be destroyed.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Honored One who subdues the three realms,
the Supreme Great Vajra, uttered these words:
"Up until the vidyādhara, through the perfection of the three vajra-wisdoms and attaining union in the two places, one accomplishes all matters of offering.
This is the accomplishment of all Buddhas, the dharma of the great mantra-samādhi."
Entering the mastery of the Vidyārājñī, one should visualize the union with Vajra.
When this rite is accomplished, it is called the Samaya Maṇḍala.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi and all the Tathāgatas are born [therefrom].
The Buddhas performed the great empowerment and further spoke these words:
“All those worlds are summoned by means of these Dharma verses;
abiding in union with the Great Seal, one accomplishes all activities.”
The Buddha’s true transformation consists of countless billions of vajras;
this is called the Buddha-Bhagavān, the dharma of the bodhi-samādhi.
Having attained the accomplishment of bodhi, one manifests the signs of the three vajras.
"Entering the Vajra Mahāsattva, The ocean of the supreme bodhicitta. Chapter Eleven:

The Section on the Supreme Vidyādhara Mahāsattva of the True Samādhi of All Tathāgatas. From the *Assembly of All Buddhas*, the most profound secret within secrets of the supreme vajra-body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas: At that time, the Bhagavān Vairocana-vajra-tathāgata entered the samādhi of the Supreme Vajra-vidyādhara Mahāsattva of all Tathāgatas.
Emerging from meditative absorption, he proclaimed the supreme mantra-words of the great vidyā-vajra of all Tathāgatas:
"One should establish the supreme great mudrā of the three vajra-syllables in the equality of all bodhi through the vajra of great wisdom—namely:
the syllable Oṃ is the root of wisdom, which is the equality of the body-vajra;..."
The syllable *A* is the selflessness of phenomena (*dharmanairātmya*), which is the equality of Vāgvajra;

the syllable *Hūṃ* is the indestructible, which is the equality of Cittavajra—thus, by abiding in the firmness of the equality of these three vajras, one is the Great Vidyādhara arising from the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
"One should visualize this syllable *bhrūṃ* (the same applies to the following), which immediately becomes the heart maṇḍala of the Vajra of Space, surrounded on all sides by all vajras."
Within that, one further visualizes a vast cloud of vajra-wisdom; this syllable *bhrūṃ* is the heart of vajra-wisdom.
Furthermore, one visualizes these syllables *hūṃ* and *oṃ*, which form the vajra-maṇḍala of the respective family, with all its characteristics perfectly complete.
Furthermore, one should visualize this syllable *Aṃ*, which becomes the maṇḍala of the primary deity, with all the characteristics of the primary deity and the noble deities fully perfected.
Furthermore, one should visualize this syllable *Hūṃ* and the syllable *A*, which become the dharma-maṇḍala.

"Among all such syllables, one should know that the syllable *bhrūṃ* is the characteristic of non-abiding; it is born from the visualization of the three vajras. These are called the heart-syllables of the Vajra Secret Samādhi, and they are also the most supreme body, speech, and mind of the Buddhas of the three times."
"The syllable Oṃ is the most supreme body of all Buddhas; the syllable Aṃ is the true speech of all Buddhas; and the syllable ĀḤ is the great wisdom-mind of all Buddhas."

"Furthermore, the syllable HŪṂ is also unsurpassed enlightenment; it is the unsurpassed enlightenment of all Tathāgatas, which accomplishes the vajra of non-conceptual wisdom of the noble Dharma. It gives birth to the Vidyādharas who are the true cause and fruit of all Buddhas. In this way, one attains the accomplishment of the supreme renown and the practice of the Great Mantra (Mahāvidyā), directly realizing the samādhi-dharmas. The three types of vajras are firm, indestructible, and unbreakable. This is called the Samādhi-dharma of the True Cause of the Vajra Empowerment of the Reality-Wisdom of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas; this dharma can accomplish all that is practiced."

"If there be a practitioner who cultivates this dharma, dwelling in a secluded place in meditative equipoise and visualizing the aforementioned syllables as before, that person will swiftly accomplish the three vajra-kāyas within half a month."

"Furthermore, the practitioner should abide in space and visualize the supreme maṇḍala of the Vajra Tathāgata arising from the root vidyā-mantra. The Vidyādhara Mahāsattva utters the syllable *Oṃ*, whereby the heart becomes a maṇḍala from which five kinds of great clouds of light emerge. Within this, one visualizes the supreme Mahāvairocana Tathāgata, who further manifests countless Buddha-bodies; the vajra-light universally illumines all things. This is called the Samādhi Dharma of the Vajra-Light Ornamentation of the Secret Body, Speech, and Mind Activities of All Tathāgatas."

If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, within half a month they will swiftly attain the supreme and most excellent body; equal to the body of a Buddha, it shall be firm and indestructible, they shall abide for three kalpas, and they will sport without hindrance amidst the five sensory objects.

"Furthermore, the practitioner should abide in space and visualize the supreme Vajra Dharma Maṇḍala arising from the root *mahāvidyā*. The Vidyādhara Mahāsattva proclaims that the letter *A* forms the maṇḍala, manifesting the five-colored light-rays of the Great Vajra. Within this, one should visualize the Tathāgata Amitāyus emerging from the Samādhi of Equal Wisdom and Right Speech, proclaiming the words of the True Dharma, free from all conceptual proliferation—a vajra verbal activity that is equal and firm. This is called the Dharma of the Samādhi Arising from the Vajra Right Speech of All Tathāgatas."

If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, they will immediately achieve accomplishment in the adamantine activity of speech, abide for three kalpas, and move unimpededly through the five sensory objects as they please.

"Furthermore, the practitioner should abide in space and visualize the supreme Vajra Maṇḍala arising from the root vidyā-mantra. The Vidyādhara Mahāsattva utters the syllable *HŪṂ*, whereby the maṇḍala is formed within the heart, manifesting the fivefold light of the vast and true samādhi. Within this, one visualizes the Great Wisdom Vajra Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata, the supreme non-abiding of all vajras. From the Vajra-heart, he gives rise to the samādhi that accomplishes the ocean of merit of all-knowledge; as the Great Guide, he generates correct wisdom. This is called the Supreme Samādhi Dharma of the Great Heart Secret Vajra of All Tathāgatas."

If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, they will immediately achieve the adamantine mind-activity, abide for three kalpas, and sport without hindrance in accordance with the five sensory objects.

Furthermore, the practitioner should abide in empty space and visualize the syllable *Khaṃ*, thereby forming the Great Vajra Samatājñāna Maṇḍala. Manifesting all bodies equal to the realm of empty space, they all arise from the equality of vajra wisdom. In an instant, one transforms vast offerings to all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas; this is called the Samādhi Dharma of the Ornamented Radiant Garland of the Anuttara Body, Speech, and Mind of the Space-Equivalent Vajra Samaya.
If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, they will immediately attain the *kalpa-sthiti-samādhi*, which even the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas cannot perceive.

Furthermore, the practitioner should abide in space and visualize the Vajra Maṇḍala arising from the root *mahāvidyā*. The *Vidyādhara-mahāsattva* utters the syllable *HŪṂ*; the mind becomes the maṇḍala, manifesting vajras and other forms that emit various radiances. Within this, one further visualizes the Honored One Mañjuśrī; this is the *sambhogakāya* abiding in the vajra-samādhi of the activities of body, speech, and mind. Having long since dwelt in the ten stages (*daśabhūmi*) of a Bodhisattva, this is called the "Dharma of the Vajra-Samādhi of the Bodhisattva Supreme Wisdom Moon."
If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, they will immediately attain all accomplishments.

Furthermore, the practitioner should abide in space and visualize this syllable *saphiliṃ* (pronounced with a long vowel). From within this syllable, the light of wisdom emerges; from within that light, the body of Vajrasattva appears, equal in measure to space. This is called the Samādhi Dharma of the Array of the Vajra-Samādhi Equal to the Realm of Space.

If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, they will attain the five supernormal powers as well as the power of the Buddha’s supreme samādhi; such is called the accomplishment of all things.

"Furthermore, the practitioner should abide in space and visualize the syllable *Oṃ*. This immediately constitutes the supreme Buddha-maṇḍala. Within it, one should visualize Akṣobhya Tathāgata appearing, followed by the appearance of all Vajrapuruṣas. One should visualize that Akṣobhya Buddha manifests as the mark of wisdom, all of which is born from the samādhi of the three vajras of Akṣobhya Tathāgata’s meditative concentration. This is called the Dharma of the Supreme Vajra Samādhi for the Direct Realization of Bodhi through the Samaya-body of Akṣobhya Tathāgata."

If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, they will immediately achieve the samādhi of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya; their body, speech, and mind will abide eternally in adamantine firmness, and they will accomplish all vajra-offering activities throughout the worlds of the ten directions.

"Furthermore, the practitioner should abide in space and visualize the syllable OṂ. This immediately forms the supreme Buddha-maṇḍala. Within it, one visualizes the manifestation of Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata and Ākāśavajra. One visualizes that Ratnasaṃbhava Buddha manifests his jewel-mark; all of these arise from the samādhi of the three vajras of the meditative concentration of Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata. This is called the Dharma of the Supreme Vajra Samādhi of Sovereignty over the Jewel Samādhi."

If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, they will immediately achieve the adamantine three karmas of Ratnasambhava Tathāgata; they will manifest the equal radiance of the jewel-banner and accomplish the dharma of bodhi, the wisdom of non-self, and the secret, equanimous mark of non-abiding.

"Furthermore, the practitioner should abide in space and visualize the syllable *Oṃ*. This immediately constitutes the supreme Buddha-maṇḍala. Within it, one should visualize the appearance of Tathāgata Amitāyus performing the mudrā of bestowing the Dharma. From the three vajra samādhis and the samaya of Tathāgata Amitāyus, the equality of the three kinds of vajra nectar is produced. This is called the Samādhi-dharmaparyāya of the Auspicious Vajra Radiance of Immeasurable Merit."

If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, they will immediately achieve the immeasurable body, speech, and mental activities of Amitāyus, and further attain the equal radiance of vajra-life, enabling them to expound the Mahāyāna path for the sake of sentient beings.

"Furthermore, the practitioner should abide in space and visualize the syllable Oṃ. This immediately forms the supreme Buddha-maṇḍala, from which appears a great blue vajra lotus. Within it, one should visualize the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi manifesting the signs of samādhi. He emerges from the equality of the three-vajra meditative concentration and samādhi of the Tathāgata Amoghasiddhi; this is called the Samādhi-dharma of the Emergence of Supreme Wisdom through the Radiance of the Amoghasiddhi-samādhi."

If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, they will accomplish the non-empty vajra activities of body, speech, and mind; they will attain the vajra non-empty, equal radiance, give birth to the auspicious ocean of wisdom, and benefit all sentient beings.

"Furthermore, the practitioner should abide in space and visualize the syllable OṂ. This immediately forms the maṇḍala of the Buddha of Radiance. Within it, one should visualize the appearance of Tathāgata Vairocana manifesting the marks of the three bodies, emitting great adamantine light. All of this arises equally from the samādhi of the three adamantine meditations of Tathāgata Vairocana. This is called the method of the supreme adamantine samādhi for seeking the body, speech, and mind of Bodhi."

If there are practitioners who cultivate this dharma, they will immediately achieve the Vairocana-vajra of the three karmas, attain the great bodhi-wisdom of equal radiance, and accomplish the indestructible stability of the three bodies.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again spoke in verse:
"Those who practice the Dharma Should arouse a mind of diligence And go to the mountains,
Or to wildernesses and empty dwellings."
And on the banks of both rivers, in places such as the Śītavana cemetery,
one should abide with a mind in meditative concentration and perform the rites according to one's aim.
One should abide within the realm of space and visualize the wisdom of Akṣobhya and the others.
Associated with the fivefold supernormal powers, one should visualize the Buddha in the supreme state;
this is called the Great Samādhi of all Buddhas,
which accomplishes all matters— the Great Vajra Wisdom-Power.
The five-pronged vajra, adorned with five flames of light, Corresponds in all five places;
from it, the vajra-attainment is born.
Visualize yourself as the Great Wheel, With fierce flames and a blazing mass of consciousness.
Through union with the fivefold supernormal powers, one accomplishes the vajra-supernormal power.
Visualizing the empty vajra-wheel, the light of the Buddhas of equality appears;
abiding in the yoga of the Buddha, one attains equality with the Buddha-body.
Visualize within the maṇḍala that one’s own body becomes Vairocana,
abiding with the syllable Oṃ at the heart.
From the mind of the quiescent vajra, there is constant production.
The jewel that fulfills all wishes and brings auspiciousness, The supreme accomplishment of all Buddhas.
Visualize again the maṇḍala, In its center appears the Honored One Akṣobhya,
Abiding in the heart-syllable *HŪṂ*, Manifesting the form of a moon at his heart.
Again, visualize the maṇḍala, in the center of which appears Amitāyus,
abiding in the heart-syllable *A*, manifesting the form of a vajra-moon.
This most supreme samādhi is indestructible through the three vajras.
Through the wisdom of the samādhi of quiescence, the Buddha achieves equality.
Abiding within the realm of space, one visualizes one’s own maṇḍala;
with the syllable Oṃ as body, speech, and mind, one dwells steadfastly for an eon.
Visualize within the expanse of space the Vajra Maṇḍala;
with the body, speech, and mind of the syllable HŪṂ, it remains steadfast for one kalpa.
Within the realm of empty space, one visualizes the Dharma-maṇḍala;
with the syllable A as body, speech, and mind, it remains steadfast for an eon.
"Thus, this is called the Samādhi of the Wisdom of the Three Kalpas of the Vajra of All Buddhas.

If one attains correspondence with this Dharma, one immediately accomplishes the vajra activities of body, speech, and mind; abiding in a firm body, speaking according to reality, and free from all false conceptualizations, one immediately attains the accomplishment of Vajrasattva."
The *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-mahāyogatantra-rāja*, Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll Second.
The *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-mahāyogatantra-rāja*,
Spoken by the Buddha, Scroll Third.

At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva, the supreme teacher of the world, who has accomplished the most excellent wisdom, translated the scriptures in the Western Heaven [India] as the Chao Feng Da Fu and Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
The Samādhi of the Three Vajras, born of true wisdom,
proclaims the methods of accomplishment from the activity of vajra speech:
"The samādhi equal to space, whose intrinsic nature is free from doubt."
The naturally pure dharma is what is called the *nāṭaka* visualization.
Those who wish to perform the rites should go to a wilderness,
a mountain range, a forest, or a place where flowers and fruits flourish.
One should visualize the syllable *maṃ*, which becomes the body of Mañjuśrī;
abiding in the three vajra activities, it is vast and without limit.
Measuring one hundred yojanas in breadth, it blazes with intense vajra light.
Within the light appear all manner of signs, adorned with every ornament;
yet even Brahmā, Śakra, and the like cannot perceive his body.
This is named Mañjuśrī, the supreme Vajra-samādhi.
The *āntardhāna* rite is the supreme *samādhi*.
If one wishes to accomplish this rite, one should combine the five kinds of nectar with the three types of iron to fashion a *yogīraja*.
The indestructible three vajras, born from the three vajras—
those who accomplish this dharma obtain the *āṭopana*.
Visualizing it within one's own heart, it is indestructible even by all the Buddhas.
In a single instant, Mañjuśrī appears;
all Buddhas, being without abiding marks, dwell in the equality of the Buddhas.
Visualizing [him] arising from the luminosity of one’s own mind, he is born from the dharma of his own family.
Manifesting three hundred and sixty great wheels as vast as Mount Sumeru,
even numbering as many as atoms, all those blazing vajra-wheels abide therein.
"This is called the Samādhi-dharmā of the Vajracakra-samaya.
Furthermore, from the heart-mantra, one should visualize the appearance of a great vajra abiding within the maṇḍala;
it is the vajra of the characteristic of non-abiding."
The mind-vajra is equanimous, manifesting thirty-six hundred [forms],
each as vast as Mount Sumeru, even unto the number of atoms;
they are exquisite yojanas in measure, with all marks perfectly complete.
Within the three realms, he is the supreme Vajra;
to that Lord Rudra, all pay homage.
This is called the Dharma of the Samādhi of Vajra Equality.
Furthermore, one should visualize the luminosity of one's own mind as an eight-petaled vajra-lotus;
all phenomena lack a fixed abiding nature, and the dharmas of the mind are likewise equal.
Within it appear thirty-six hundred [petals], each as vast as Mount Sumeru.
"Even as numerous as atoms, with pure jewel lotuses,
one makes offerings to all Buddhas in the supreme maṇḍala.
This is called the Lotus Equality Samādhi Dharma."
Abiding in the samādhi of three kalpas, In accordance with the five kinds of wisdom,
One performs the service of the three secrets To all Buddhas of the ten directions.
Through the visualization of one’s own vidyā, The sword manifests five kinds of light.
Once the practitioner has grasped this, they shall attain mastery over the Vidyādharas.
They will receive the great offerings of the three realms; Brahmā and others shall take refuge in them.
They are the courageous ones of the trichiliocosm, the most supreme and secret Honored Ones.
With mastery over whatever actions one desires, one attains the three vajra activities;
by visualizing the mind-vajra, such accomplishment is bestowed.
This is called the Samādhi Method for the Accomplishment of the Vajra Sword.
"One should visualize the syllable Oṃ, which becomes a *kūrca* the size of a *jñānaka*;
within it appears the form of the deity,
upon which one should fix the mind and meditate."
In an instant, the practitioner becomes equal to all the Bodhisattvas;
like the sun shining in the void, his body possesses the marks of a purple-golden hue.
Furthermore, by visualizing the syllable A, he likewise becomes a *ūrṇā* (the hair-tuft between the eyebrows).
Within the measure of a *jñānaka*, one visualizes the image of the central deity;
dwelling the mind in contemplation,
the practitioner in an instant accomplishes the wisdom of enlightenment.
Like the sun shining in the void, his body possesses the marks of a purple-gold color.
Furthermore, one should visualize the syllable HŪṂ, which likewise becomes a *yūlika* [lotus] the size of a *jñānaka*;
within it appears the image of the Principal Deity.
Abiding in the mind, one performs the visualization.
In an instant, the practitioner accomplishes the vajra-body,
like the sun shining in the sky, with a body of purple-golden hue.
One should dwell in the visualization of emptiness;
within the maṇḍala of the Knowledge of All Modes, the Honored One Vairocana appears. Visualize him holding a great wheel;
through the accomplishment of the vidyā-mantra of the wheel, he abides in the Wheel Family.
This accomplishment of supreme wisdom is born from vajra-wisdom;
such a body of the Great Wheel is accomplished through union.
One should abide in the contemplation of emptiness and visualize the vajra maṇḍala.
In the center appears the Honored One Akṣobhya, holding a vajra in his hand;
the Great Vajra Vidyādhara, abiding in the Vajra Family,
the supreme accomplishment of the Vajra, born from Vajra Wisdom.
Thus, this vajra body is accomplished through union.
One should abide in the meditation on emptiness and visualize a maṇḍala of various jewels;
in its center appears the Honored One Ratnasambhava, visualized holding a wondrous jewel in his hand.
The Vidyādhara Mahāratnasaṃbhava abides in the Mahāratnakula;
through the supreme ratna-siddhi born of vajra-wisdom,
such a mahāratna-body is accomplished through union.
Abiding in the midst of empty space, one should visualize the Dharma-maṇḍala;
therein appears Amitāyus, holding a great lotus.
This Great Lotus Vidyādhara dwells within the Lotus Family.
The supreme accomplishment of the lotus, born from the wisdom of the vajra—
such is the wondrous dharmakāya, accomplished through union.
One should abide in emptiness and visualize the samādhi maṇḍala.
Amoghasiddhi appears, holding a great, sharp sword;
this vidyādhara of the great, sharp sword abides in the Samaya family.
Through the supreme accomplishment of samaya, he is born from vajra-wisdom.
In this manner, this great samādhi is accomplished through union.
All accomplishments— such as the trident, the hook, and so forth—
which are performed according to the ritual method, result in the attainment of vajra-union.
Abiding in a mind of meditative concentration, the three karmas are all accomplished;
this is what is called the Buddhas, the Great Vajra Samādhi.
Furthermore, the method of accomplishment is taught: for all those who perform the rites,
One should go to a crossroads or beneath a solitary tree to perform the vajra-invocation,
summoning the deities of one's own sacred field. Then,
following the ritual procedures, one should seek accomplishment according to one’s wishes.
The three correspondences of the Great Illumination, the supreme triple vajra,
summon the body, speech, and mind— the great wisdom of all Buddhas—
within the wind-wheel maṇḍala; this is the Buddha’s supreme summoning.
Born from the samādhi of the ten directions, it is able to summon all;
abiding in the samādhi of the perception of emptiness, it is the Vajra method of summoning.
The Honored One Vairocana is that supreme Great Wheel.
The Buddha performs the invocation without abiding, [summoning] Vajra, Padma, and the others.
Regarding the dharmas of that Samaya Family: abiding in the samādhi of the triple world, endowed with all marks, one should visualize the image of the Buddha.
Having accomplished body, speech, and mind, through the visualization of summoning and so forth,
and by means of countless practices of union, one skillfully accomplishes all activities.
He is fully endowed with all marks; visualizing his body as vajra, his tongue is in union with vajra, and his speech is equal to vajra.
This offering of the three secrets is supreme among all offerings.
This is the secret, exquisite Dharma of all Buddhas.
This is called the Great Secret Mantra of the Buddhas’ Samādhi of Summoning.

If there are practitioners seeking various accomplishments, they should maintain the visualization of samādhi while partaking of the five kinds of food and drink; such a person will immediately attain the accomplishment of a Vidyādhara, possess the five supernatural powers and the *āntardhāna* (power of invisibility), and achieve the vajra-summoning of all accomplishments.

If one cannot obtain all five kinds of food, yet dwells in samādhi by obtaining even a single meal, this person will immediately attain the supreme correspondence (*yoga*), be empowered by all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas, possess all marks, have the vajra-solidity of body, speech, and mind, achieve the equality of mental wisdom, wear the vajra crown, and hold the supreme dhāraṇī.

All those Buddhas, through this same samādhi, are able to perform the supreme samādhi and all accomplishments for the sake of others; this is called the Dharma of the Samādhi of the Vajra of All-Equivalent Wisdom.
Furthermore, the supreme method for accomplishing the samādhi of the three vajras shall be proclaimed.
One should visualize the syllable HŪṂ upon one’s own tongue; this is the supreme vajra-samādhi.
In this way, the tongue faculty is endowed with the five kinds of nectar and attains the indestructible nature of the three vajras.

Furthermore, one should know that the syllables *A* and *Ṭha* constitute the supreme vajra of various correspondences; through them, one achieves the accomplishment of Vajrasattva. This is called the method of the samādhi of the Vajra Nectar Samaya.

Furthermore, those who practice the supreme accomplishment of the Samādhi of the Three Vajras shall immediately attain the supreme accomplishment of the three vajra-bodies. The ocean of wish-fulfilling jewels of the Buddhas of the ten directions emits pure light that pervades all worlds; such is the mastery of the Vajra.

Furthermore, for one who practices the supreme accomplishment of the Wheel Samādhi, there is the accomplishment of practicing in accordance with the equality of all phenomena. One becomes a great sovereign over all samādhis as numerous as the sands of the Ganges and all supreme vidyādhara methods; one perfects all excellent and wondrous samādhis, dwells in the perception of the vajra-body, and attains the mastery of *antardhāna* (invisibility). Emitting a thousand rays of light in all directions, one is fully endowed with all methods of accomplishment. All worldly beings—the asuras, gandharvas, and the entire host of gandharvas—all pay homage and submit, being gathered under one's influence. One abides well in the non-abiding mark of the three vajras of all Tathāgatas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; this is called Vajra Accomplishment.

"With the vajra-eye one perceives all things universally; just as one performs all manner of activities with one's own hands according to one's will, so too is the observation and penetration of that vajra-eye."

Furthermore, emitting great sounds throughout buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they turn the wheel of the ultimate meaning so that it is heard everywhere and by all; thus accomplishing the ultimate meaning of the adamantine faculty of hearing, this is the adamantine activity of speech.

Furthermore, one can accomplish the vajra-mind-action, thoroughly comprehending the mental activities and all other phenomena of sentient beings within buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges; this is called the vajra-mind-action.

Furthermore, one can emanate from that nāṭaka as many bodies as there are grains of sand in the Ganges, dwelling within the kalpas of saṃsāra, manifesting the adornment of clouds of Buddhas, and performing various transformations as the supreme vajra-birth; this is called the vajra-activity of body, which is also the dharma of vajra-supernormal powers.
Furthermore, one is able to recollect all phenomena of the past through the power of samādhi; this is called the "Vajra Recollection of the Past.

Such qualities as these are termed the vajra eyes, ears, and mind, the recollection of the past, and the accomplishment of supernormal powers (*abhijñā*) through samādhi. The supernormal powers of all Buddhas are equally accomplished within the bodies of all Buddhas. Constantly surrounded by a retinue equal in number to the sands of the Ganges, they skillfully perform the vajra activities of body, speech, and mind. In all worlds, they accord with and accomplish the vajra samādhi, thereby giving rise to the accomplishment of great benefit and attaining the perfection of the four kinds of samādhi.

"Having fully understood the indestructible activity of the vajra, one performs the visualization corresponding to the samādhi of compliant practice, thereby accomplishing supreme enlightenment and cultivating the supreme accomplishment of supramundane dharmas. Entering the Vajrayāna, one practices all dharmas in accordance with them and proclaims the great mantras."

Through sovereign visualization, one achieves great accomplishment; relying on the proper time and according to the ritual method, one visualizes the image of a vajra from one's own *vidyā*, wears a vajra crown, and assumes the posture of sovereignty, thereby attaining the accomplishment of the Great Wisdom Vajra.
In all places, one should constantly draw near to the nectar-like Dharma of wisdom; this is called the accomplishment of the true meaning within all great vidyās.

If a practitioner would cultivate this, they should first select a location according to the ritual—whether it be a vast wilderness, a mountain range, or a secluded place—and perform the various accomplishments according to the prescribed procedures. Furthermore, by never allowing for interruption at any time, one will attain all accomplishments; this is known as the Great Accomplishment Method of all Buddhas.

"Furthermore, the practitioner should constantly draw near to the four kinds of adamantine, firm activities; by visualizing the bodies of the three vajras, one will swiftly attain accomplishment, corresponding with those four periods according to the ritual method."

"Furthermore, having understood the five locations according to the Dharma, one establishes a time limit—whether seven days, half a month, or even a month—and visualizes the syllable Oṃ according to the ritual procedures, thereby becoming a Wisdom Vajra. Within that, the Vajra Samādhi arises, as extensively explained in the various ritual manuals."

“Those who practice the yoga methods should understand the divisions of days, months, and times as they truly are, so as not to transgress the dharma; by doing so, they shall attain the supreme secret accomplishment that accords with the arising of ultimate reality.”
Furthermore, the verses on the accomplishment of the Buddha-body, the supreme realm of the supramundane Dharma, are proclaimed as follows:
“The Buddha-body is the most supreme, upholding auspiciousness; The three vajras are indestructible.
Abiding in the empowerment of secret syllables, It skillfully creates the indestructible vajra body.”
All Tathāgatas of the ten directions, whose three secrets are indestructible vajras,
abide in the secret phrases of empowerment and perfectly manifest the supreme vajra body.
Furthermore, he spoke these verses on the accomplishment of the Buddha’s words regarding the supreme realm of the supramundane Dharma:
“The Dharma-words of all Buddhas are of great auspiciousness; The three vajras are indestructible.
Abiding in the secret phrases of empowerment, One skillfully enters the gateway of the vajra Dharma-words.”
All Tathāgatas of the ten directions, whose three vajras are indestructible,
abide in the secret phrases of empowerment, which have arisen from the true speech of the Buddha.
Furthermore, he spoke these verses on the accomplishment of the Buddha-mind, the supreme realm of supramundane phenomena:
"The Buddha-mind is the auspicious holder of the vajra; The three vajras are indestructible.
Abiding in the empowerment of secret syllables, One dwells well in the vast vajra mind."
All the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, whose threefold vajras are indestructible,
abide in the secret phrases of empowerment, which are born from the dharmas of the Buddha’s mind.
The speech of the Buddha is the speech of the Vajra Dharma; the speech of Vajrasattva is likewise so.
If one who lacks wisdom transgresses the ritual procedures, all of that will be utterly destroyed.

**Chapter Thirteen: The Section on the Samādhi of Right Knowledge through the True Visualization of the Vajra-Related Adornment Samādhi, from the Supreme and Most Profound Secret within Secrets, the Great Assembly of All Tathāgatas’ Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind.** At that time, the Vajradhara—the supreme wisdom, the source of all true meanings—the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, prostrated with his head at the feet of all the Great Teachers, the Munis; he paid homage to the Lord of the True Knowledge of the Samādhi of the Solidification of All Meanings, and uttering a vajra-sound, spoke these words:
“How marvelous! The Buddha-teaching!”
How great is Great Enlightenment!
How great is the Dharma of Quiescence!
How great is the Practice of True Words!
Ultimate non-arising phenomena, whose self-nature is without birth, dwell in reality free from doubt, produced by right wisdom.
This is what all Buddhas have taught: the dharma of all luminous phrases.
The vajra-wisdom offering, the indestructibility of the three vajras;
that which is attained through the wisdom of all Buddhas, the visualization of the three vajras,
and the great correspondence of recitation— all these are empowered by all Buddhas.
The mantra syllables of all the families abide in the characteristics of body, speech, and mind;
by hearing the great sound that upholds the great vidyā, one enters the ocean of wisdom.
From the Buddhas of the three times arise the great vajra of the three activities.
"Attain peerless wisdom, And visualize the Vajra-vidyā.
Furthermore, O Vajrapāṇi!

The recitation of all Vajradharas emerges from the three vajra-minds.

this is the supreme secret dharma, the ritual procedure for the sublime offering.

Body, speech, and mind are without self; Abide in the mind of vast wisdom.

this is all Buddhas, As observed by the eye of wisdom.

The bodhi of the mind-samādhi abides in the practice of the vajra-mind;
this is called Vajra Mind; such is the recitation of mind.
Reciting in accordance with all meanings, it is not something practiced by way of intrinsic nature;
the Buddhas of the three times are likewise so—such is the precious recitation.
The body manifests clouds of transformations, pervading all Buddha-fields.
Firm and without coming or going, it is called the "Non-empty Recitation.
This secret mantra-phrase, the most supreme meaning of syllables,
emits a vast sound that is heard throughout the maṇḍala.
All wrathful dharmas are born from the wisdom of samādhi;
the recitation of those wrathful ones is thus explained as secret.
Sentient beings dwell in the ocean of delusion, revolving according to the objects of their various desires.
To thoroughly understand all places is the recitation of the Buddha Family;
Sentient beings dwell in an ocean of desire, and from the Vajra of Desire speech arises;
Likewise, when body and mind abide [in that state], it is the recitation of the Lotus Family.
Sentient beings dwell in anger; from the mind of the Vajra of Anger, body and speech likewise abide. This is the recitation of the Vajra Family.
Within the Samādhi of the Three Vajras, amidst the Vajra Samādhi,
Thus, through the *nāmasaṃgīti* dharma of all these Vajras,
the Lord of All Secrets realizes the true meaning of the dharma of desire:
that enlightenment is born from desire, and so it is for all sentient beings as well.
The great vidyā-mantras such as Buddha-eye always follow and transform the phenomena of desire,
accomplishing mastery over desire and proceeding in accordance with all paths of the mind;
from the equality of the phenomena of delusion, the Vajra-holder Vidyārāja arises.
That Napaṃsaka bestows the supreme accomplishment;
born from the wrathful dharma of aversion, he is ever like one who destroys enemies.
Though born, he does not abide, thereby accomplishing the supreme dharma.
"This is called the Samādhi of the Great Beings of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, the meaning of the great mantras of the five Buddhas and their respective families shall be explained.
One should abide within the mind-cakra and visualize the cakra of great wisdom."
Regarding the Great Wheel Maṇḍala, one should contemplate the meaning of the Great Wheel Vidyā.
Abiding in the vajra-mind, one should visualize the Wisdom-Vajra;
regarding the Vajra Maṇḍala, one should contemplate the meaning of the Vajra Vidyā.
Abiding in the mind of the Ratna family, one should visualize the great wisdom-jewel and the maṇḍala of all jewels,
contemplating the meaning of the vidyā-mantra of all jewels.
Abiding in the mind of the Padma family, one should visualize the lotus-wisdom.
In the maṇḍala of the supreme dharma, one should contemplate the meaning of the lotus vidyā.
Abiding in the mind of samādhi, one should visualize the wisdom of samādhi;
in the maṇḍala of samādhi, one should contemplate the meaning of the samādhi vidyā.
Within all maṇḍalas, the five Buddha-Bhagavāns are arrayed;
they manifest five kinds of light, emanated by the wisdom of bodhi.
These vast vidyās follow and turn according to various meanings.
The three vajras are indestructible; gradually expanding and then gradually contracting,
the body abides in the self-nature of the body, the mind abides in the own-characteristic of the mind,
and speech abides in correct speech, thereby attaining the supreme offering.
In the great wheel maṇḍala, one should visualize the five kinds of vajras;
in its center appears the Lord of Secrets, along with the images of the deities and so forth.
The vidyās of the various families and the four types of maṇḍalas [are likewise visualized].
There are four kinds of colors; contemplate the meaning of the heart-mantra (cittavijñāna).
The activities of the four vajras are the deeds of the fixed vajra.
All these great mantras (mahāvidyā) are the supreme, secret, and eternally abiding.
One should know that all rites for pacification possess the marks of Buddhalocanā;
those for increase possess the marks of Padmavajrī;
and all rites for magnetizing manifest the marks of Viśvavajrī.
Among all methods of subduing, there is the form of the Vajra Wrathful One.
Within all these teachings, there are the three secrets and the three bodies.
Among all great mantras, one should visualize the form of Nāṭaka.
Furthermore, if one wishes to achieve accomplishment within this world,
with the exception of those who are unfilial, those who slander their ācāryas,
and those who are most extremely wicked— among all such classes of sentient beings, [one should not practice].
"Though one seeks with courageous diligence, one cannot achieve it.
This is called the Samādhi of the Great Vajra Wisdom Wheel of all Buddhas.
All sentient beings of the three realms should dwell in the visualization of the Buddha-body."
Destroying all enemies, each and every task shall be accomplished.
Visualize within the sky a great wheel, five-spoked and four-faced,
complete with all its characteristics.
Visualize Vajrasattva arising from samādhi.
Visualize the wheel of the Buddhas of the three times, turning clockwise with the right hand—the great powerful wheel of all Buddhas.
The sentient beings of the ten directions are born from the Buddha’s vast body;
through their harmonious union, they enter entirely into one's own self.
Furthermore, there arise transformations that produce the vajra-wisdom of all Buddhas.
Wrathful, belonging to the wrathful family, with a most fierce and terrifying appearance;
Vajrapāṇi in his wrathful form, wielding various weapons and implements,
giving rise to thoughts of destroying evil, he shatters all who are greatly wicked.
The supreme three bodies of all Buddhas, the realm of the three vajras,
bestow all accomplishments and deliver beings from the darkness of ignorance;
by performing the rite within seven days, one will certainly achieve success in all things.
"This is called the Samādhi-Practice of the Great Vajradhara of All Buddhas, the Vajra-Wisdom Wheel.
Dwelling in the thought of the great wheel within emptiness, adorned with vajra-light,
one should visualize the Honored One Vairocana in its center, complete with all marks."
Born from the Samādhi of the Three Times, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Loving One, holds in his hand a vajra blazing with light; one should visualize him thus.
All sentient beings of the ten directions are born from the vajra-body.
Through that union and correspondence, one enters completely into one's own body.
Listen attentively to the command of all Buddhas: through the correspondence of body, speech, and mind, there is the supreme vajra-binding, from which wisdom arises as transformation.
"O Śrī-Vajrapāṇi, this is the supreme Great Samaya.
Should anyone violate this, they shall certainly be destroyed.
This is called the Vajra-Mahācakra-Buddhājñā-Samaya-Samādhi-practice."
Abiding in the visualization of the Vajra, within the Buddha-maṇḍala,
are the Great Wheel of the Wrathful Kings and the deities such as the Vajras.
All classes of sentient beings are born from the Buddhas of the three times.
The bodies of those sentient beings enter the maṇḍala of the three bodies.
From this, all Buddhas further arise through transformation;
that Yamāntaka is the form of the wrathful vidyārāja.
All sentient beings of the three periods of time, Giving rise to hearts of great enmity and malice, Are visualized as being destroyed by wrath; They enter the Vajra of Great Wisdom.
"This is called the Dharma of the Samādhi of the Vajra-Wisdom of the Three Bodies of the Wrathful King Yamāntaka, born from all Samādhis."
"The vajras of body, speech, and mind, the merit of the meaning of self-luminosity,
are the supreme samādhi, as turned according to the Buddha’s command."
The Great Illumination of Meaning acts as protection;
it is the victorious Vajra-wisdom body. All those Vajras protect the meaning of Bodhi.
This is called the Samādhi of the Three Vajras of all Buddhas.
"Abiding in the midst of space, one should visualize the Great Dharma-Vajra,
the Buddha Vairocana, born from the supreme body.
That samādhi of the three bodies is the ritual procedure of Heṣasana."
One should abide in the realm of empty space and visualize all Buddhas as pervading it; through the wisdom of the self-luminous syllables, one contemplates the manifestation of the mental image.
Then, gradually condensing the Buddhas, one contemplates the great luminosity of the mind.
The acts of the Mind-Vajra pervade the three bodies.
This is called "The Samādhi Method of the Radiant Great Mantra of the Vajra-Jewel of the Firm Three Karmas of All Buddhas."
"Visualize Vajrapāṇi, endowed with all marks;
following the path traversed by all Buddhas, proceed accordingly and in accordance with reason.
With steps that are equal and harmonious, visualize [him] from the crown of the head down to the feet."
"This is the method for the samādhi called 'The Equal-Step Forward March of the Ocean of the Self-Nature Purity of All Buddhas.
Within the outer maṇḍala, one should visualize the appearance of the Wrathful Deity,
the Vajra-karma-step, and visualize his crown-mark."
"This is the Dharma of the Samādhi of Vajra-Right-Speech, the Mantra-Syllables for Subjugating All Heretical Sorceresses of the Non-Buddhists, the Secret Lord of the Three Vajras of all Buddhas."
“Born from the three vajras, the wrathful vajra-mark appears in a deep yellow hue.
Visualize its crown as high and vast, like the king of all mountains, manifesting above all.”
The valiant armies of all Buddhas are able to subdue the hosts of other armies;

Abiding in meditative concentration and right mindfulness, Awakening all demonic adversaries—
this is called the Buddha-Bhagavān. Visualize the *huṃ* syllable as a vajra-stake,
The measure of a five-pronged vajra, appearing within the heart.

whether it be within the realms of kingdoms, or in villages, towns,

By performing the rites according to the ritual manual, one is freed from all suffering.
Visualize within the expanse of space the great five-pronged vajra;

The maṇḍalas of the ten directions possess the appearance of blazing radiance.

"Abiding in the contemplation of emptiness, one should visualize the Śāntika Maṇḍala;
within it, one should imagine the form of Vairocana abiding in one's own heart.

Furthermore, within one's own mind, visualize the appearance of a circular light;

The Samādhi of Supreme Vajra is accomplished in a single kṣaṇa.
This is called the *Sarvabuddhasamādhivyūhameghasamādhi-dharma*.
Abiding in the thought of emptiness, one visualizes a full moon and completes the outer maṇḍala.
In the center, visualize the image of the Dharma-holder, abiding within one's own mind.

Visualize the appearance of a circular halo, the radiance of the wish-fulfilling jewel.

The Supreme Seal Vajra, which accomplishes all siddhis, is the auspicious and virtuous jewel; it is the Vajra Method of Accomplishment.
This is called the Dharma-Cloud Samādhi Adornment Samādhi Method.
Abiding in the visualization of the Vajra of Emptiness, within a half-moon maṇḍala,

The Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and others fill the maṇḍala of the entirety of space.
In union with the five kinds of light, one enters the radiance of the Great Dharma;

"Obtain the joyful gift for me, the supreme great empowerment, the object of veneration and love for all worlds; appear and behold!

The Great Wrathful Vidyārāja, his body blazing with great radiance and vajra flames, manifests wrathful and majestic light;

visualize him according to the ritual manual of his own family, following the prescribed method.

imagine him appearing with three faces, manifesting the aspect that terrifies the three realms,

According to the ritual manual of one's own family, perform the visualization according to the dharma.
Furthermore, one should visualize that great wrathful vidyārāja Nīlananda, born from the three vajras.
Visualize him with three faces, his sharp fangs protruding outward;
from his body issues forth blazing light, manifesting a form that strikes terror into the three realms.
According to the ritual manual of one's own family, one should perform the visualization in accordance with the Dharma.
Furthermore, one should visualize Acala, the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja,
born from the vajra; imagine him with three faces,
manifesting a lovely and auspicious appearance, holding a sword and a noose in his hands.
According to the ritual manual of one's own family, perform the visualization in accordance with the Dharma.
Furthermore, visualize the wheel of great mantras and the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja manifesting three vajra faces,
emitting a blazing and intense radiance.
The single-syllable Great Uṣṇīṣa form manifests universal transformations;
dwelling within the maṇḍala, one should visualize it according to the ritual manual.
Furthermore, one should visualize the Great Wrathful Vidyārāja descending from the three realms.
With three faces blazing with light, manifesting a vast and terrifying form,
sustained by supreme wisdom and born of meditative concentration,
he displays the most excellent uṣṇīṣa crown and is a great mass of radiant light.
Through mastery over this samādhi, one should visualize each [deity] individually.
These ten wrathful ones, the supreme vidyārājas,
according to what is taught in the ritual manuals, possess their respective physical characteristics.
And the great vidyās of their respective families,
all manifesting wrathful forms of the Great Self-Mastery, subduing all things—

Furthermore, it is taught that samādhi is the supreme method of visualization.

The Great Sovereigns of all Buddhas, Venerated and beloved by all worlds, Are the supreme, adamantine ones;
One should perform visualization according to the rite.

Perfectly endowed with all marks, adorned with every ornament;

"Abiding in the visualization of emptiness, one should contemplate a full moon maṇḍala.

One should visualize the Vajra of Space as a solar maṇḍala.

Chapter Fourteen: The Supreme Samādhi of the King Vidyārāja Vilokita, the Unprecedented Mantra-Syllable for Body, Speech, and Mind. This is the fourteenth chapter from the *Assembly of All Tathāgatas*, the most supreme and profound secret within secrets concerning the three vajra-activities of body, speech, and mind, titled "The Supreme Samādhi of the King Vidyārāja Vilokita, the Unprecedented Mantra-Syllable for Body, Speech, and Mind. At that time, the Blessed One, the Vajra-Tathāgata Mahāvairocana—the Great Lord of Secrets of all Buddhas—entered the great samādhi known as the "Supreme Pacification Samādhi of the Vajradhara."
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he proclaimed this great vidyā-mantra of the consort of all Tathāgatas, the Bodhisattva Locanā, by means of the three vajra-actions:

“Oṃ vāgvati ruru sphara jvala tiṣṭha siddhalocani sarvārthasādhani svāhā. When this great mantra was spoken, all who heard it felt joy in their hearts; they all called to mind the Buddhas and Vajras. This great mantra can accomplish all activities, fulfill all aspirations, and act as a rite for averting calamities for the world. There is no task it cannot achieve. Even those who wish to relinquish their life-span shall regain it through the power of this mantra. This is that which has been proclaimed by the Vajra-samaya.
At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi of the Vajra-Samaya of the Equality of the Three Bodies, the Wrathful Vajra Beyond Being and Non-being.
Emerging from this concentration, he proclaimed with his vajra-body, speech, and mind this great vidyā-mantra of the foremost of all Vajradharīs, the Bodhisattva Māmakī:

“Oṃ śaṅkari śāntikari kuṭa kuṭa kuṭiṇi gata gata kuṭiṇi svāhā. When this great mantra was spoken, all the indestructible Vajrasattvas of the three vajras cast joyful glances upward toward the Buddhas; with hearts full of joy, they contemplated the Tathāgata Vajracitta, who is ever associated with the dharma of vajra protection. They were able to accomplish all activities, constantly providing vajra-guarding through great power, causing all beings everywhere to be free from fear.
At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Great Lotus Samādhi, the Contemplative Samādhi.
Emerging from concentration, he proclaimed with his vajra body, speech, and mind this Great Mantra of the White-Robed Bodhisattva, the Foremost Consort of the Samādhi of All Dharmas, saying:

“Oṃ kaci vikaci nikaci kacitkaci karuṭaviriye svāhā. When this great mantra was spoken, all the supreme Vajradharas, abiding in a state of joy, called to mind the Tathāgata Dharmavāgvajra and accomplished the vajra-increasing rite (*vṛddhi-vajra*). This mantra constantly increases the vast treasury of Dharma and is capable of accomplishing all activities; those who maintain its recitation shall swiftly attain accomplishment as Dharmavāgvajra.
At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Pervasive Vajra.
Emerging from that concentration, he proclaimed with his vajra-body, speech, and mind this Great Empowerment (Karma) Mahāsamaya Foremost Wisdom Consort, the Great Mantra of Tārā Bodhisattva:

“Oṃ tārī tuttārī ture svāhā. When this great mantra was spoken, all the Great Beings born of the Buddhas who abide in the wisdom of joy contemplated the Vajra-Tathāgata of Body. The great, heroic, and powerful armies of the Buddhas’ vajras caused all beings throughout the realms of sentient beings to universally accomplish supreme activities, and in a single instant, caused them all to be filled with reverence and love.

"If there is a practitioner who, with a pure mind, visualizes a *yūṣmadha* placed at four locations, fully adorned and complete in all its parts, appearing like that lotus flower in full bloom."

"If there is a practitioner who generates a fierce and intense resolve, and partakes of *viṣṭha* and *mahāmāṃsa* according to the ritual, they will immediately attain accomplishment in the supreme practice of the Great Mantra, such that even all Buddhas cannot perceive them."

"Furthermore, the practitioner should give rise to a fierce and intense resolve, take the three types of *maṃca*—namely *sana*, *haya*, and *mahā*—and combine them in one place; by consuming them according to the ritual method, one will immediately achieve the supreme practice, which even all Buddhas cannot perceive."

May all various activities, according to one's wishes, be fully accomplished.
The reflected image of the Vajra Dharma, the radiance of the Lotus Family,

Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, the supreme space, all dharmas of entering and awakening, and all ritual procedures:

"Furthermore, I shall proclaim the secret Vajra-karma rite for pacifying all evil afflictions.

Furthermore, the following are the supreme mantra syllables of the heart of the three families, the secret Vajradhara-mind, which proclaim the pacification of all internal and external diseases:

One should visualize the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Vajra-mahāsattvas manifesting in wrathful form to destroy all evil māras; through union with the samādhi of a concentrated mind, the *karma* of generating impartial right mindfulness arises, as in the previous great mantra (*mahā-vidyā*).

If one can recite this in conjunction [with the practice] one hundred and eight times, all will be accomplished within seven days; the ritual procedures for the Great Vidyā-mantra of one’s own mind will likewise be accomplished. At that time, Vajrapāṇi, with the hook of great wisdom and radiance,

"The various phenomena seen in dreams are, in their very nature, unborn."
The purity of intrinsic nature is the true reality; it is the vajra-nature itself.
If one should see this even in a dream, the practitioner seeking accomplishment—whether in the form of recitation or entering the method of meditative absorption—[will attain success].
One shall attain the state of a Buddha or Bodhisattva, with their forms appearing before one.
This is called the Great Dream Samādhi.
If, within a dream, one beholds the wondrous radiance of the Buddhas,
Having attained supreme enlightenment and accomplished all-knowledge,

By performing various offerings and the like,
one shall certainly achieve the five kinds of sublime joy-dharmas of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas. If,
even in a dream, one sees making offerings to the various honored images, [one will attain success].
And the Vajrasattva, the image of the Great Lord of Secrets— by beholding these,
one shall attain the wisdom of equality and the great love of the Vajradharma.
If one sees them within a dream, as well as the various marks and limbs of one's own body, [one shall likewise attain these].
One attains the secret vajra, the most supreme renown of the great vidyā-mantra.
If one sees it even in a dream, by paying homage to all the Tathāgatas and the great Bodhisattvas, one attains the adamantine firmness.
If, within a dream, one should behold all the hosts of *kinnarīs*,

One who sees such signs as these shall attain the accomplishment of their undertakings.

Giving with a joyful heart, one fulfills the treasury of the sublime Dharma.
If, even in a dream, one beholds the various Buddhas turning the wheel of Dharma,
or sees the Tathāgatas entering the state of parinirvāṇa, [one shall attain the fruit].
Having attained union with samādhi, one dwells securely in the adamantine state.
If, even in a dream, one beholds various exquisite groves and gardens,
as well as various ḍākinīs, adorned and sporting together—
Having attained the samādhi of meditative concentration, one is sustained by the empowerment of all Buddhas.
If, even in a dream, one beholds the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas,
receiving the signs of consecration and performing acts of worship;
When one accomplishes the secret, the supreme Vidyārāja,
if one beholds Caṇḍaroṣaṇa in a dream,

Such various dreams are born from the vajra;
they are the supreme accomplishment of the vajra body, speech, and mind.
These dream-activities arise from one's own mind.
If the mind abides in meditative concentration, then all phenomena abide;
because all phenomena abide, all phenomena are equal to empty space.
Being without phenomena and without the nature of phenomena, one enters the mind of samādhi.

At that time, all the Tathāgatas in the assembly, having heard Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva speak thus, marveled at this unprecedented occurrence. With their three karmas [of body, speech, and mind], they each offered praise and asked:
"How is it that dreams arise from one's own mind?"
"What is the nature of self-existence and the nature of all phenomena, and what is the true reality of all phenomena, which is like the nature of space?
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, addressed the Tathāgatas with his vajra three-karma, saying:
"Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, you should know:"
Space and all phenomena are neither conjoined nor disjoined; space has no movement, and it does not manifest anywhere, toward anything, or in any place.
“Tathāgatas, you should know:
all dream-like phenomena are likewise so; indeed, all those phenomena are equally born from within a dream.”
Just as with the Buddha, the World-Honored One, so it is with all Tathāgatas; they are identical to all phenomena, all arising equally from within a dream and dwelling in accordance with them.
“All Tathāgatas should know:
Just as space has no form or characteristics and does not appear, being without opposition and without obstruction, so too are all phenomena free from characteristics and without obstruction.”

Furthermore, it should be known that all the dharmas, as well as the vajra-samādhis of body, speech, and mind, belonging to all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas, evolve in accordance with a single, uniform nature in all places—namely, the unmoving nature of one's own mind. If body, speech, and mind abide within the Vajradhātu, they are non-dual and equal to the realm of empty space.

If all Buddhas and Tathāgatas abide in the realm of empty space, then all sentient beings likewise abide in the realm of empty space; they do not abide in the desire realm, they do not abide in the form realm, and they do not abide in the formless realm.
If phenomena do not abide anywhere within the three realms and the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, are without birth,
one should therefore know that all those phenomena lack intrinsic nature.
“Furthermore, O Tathāgatas, you should know this:
the bodhicitta that arises from the wisdom of all Tathāgatas does not abide in the body, does not abide in speech, and does not abide in the mind; therefore, bodhicitta abides nowhere at all.”
Because the bodhicitta is non-abiding, where could all phenomena abide?
Because all phenomena are non-abiding, nothing whatsoever is produced.
By virtue of this, the Great Vajra Phrase, which is the authentic wisdom of all Tathāgatas, is born.
“Furthermore, O Tathāgatas, you should know this:

that dream-like phenomenon does not appear within the triple world, it has no movement, it is unattainable, and it lacks reality. It is not characterized by a person (*puruṣa*) or the like, nor is it seen by oneself or another. Therefore, all that is produced within the triple world is like a dream; it is like what is seen in a dream, like what is born from a dream.

All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions, and even all sentient beings, are likewise thus: everything is like a dream, and no mark of a self (*ātman*) can be found. You should abide in this way.”
“Furthermore, O Tathāgatas, you should know this:

it is like a great maṇi-jewel that possesses all virtues and is the most supreme among all jewels; according to whatever beings may desire—whether gold, silver, or other treasures—it can manifest exactly what their hearts seek.”

One should know that those various jewels do not abide within the mind, nor do they abide within the maṇi-gem; all Tathāgatas, all phenomena, and all Buddha-dharmas are likewise so. All wise ones should understand it in this way.

At that time, having heard the World-Honored One, the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, speak this Dharma, all the Tathāgatas were filled with great joy; with eyes full of serene delight, they gazed upon the World-Honored One, the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, and spoke these words:
"How marvelous, World-Honored One!"
"If the realm of space abides in equality, then all phenomena and the Buddha-dharmas likewise abide in equality.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas in the assembly spoke thus:
"World-Honored One, Mahāvairocana Vajra-Tathāgata!"

I pray that you will proclaim all the great mantras and the dharmas of all vajra accomplishments; specifically, upon what do these all the great mantras and the dharmas of all vajra accomplishments abide?
At that time, the Vajradhara Mahāvairocana Vajra Tathāgata praised him, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
It is well that the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are able to inquire about this meaning."
O Great Beings, you should know this:
all great vidyās and all vajra accomplishments should abide within the vajra body, speech, and mind. Why is this?
Those great mantras, the various vajra accomplishments, and even all the Buddha-dharmas abide within one’s own body, speech, and mind.

Those three vajra activities of body, speech, and mind do not abide in the desire realm, do not abide in the form realm, and do not abide in the formless realm; they do not abide in mind and body, nor in body and mind; they do not abide in speech and mind, nor in mind and speech. Because these three activities have no place of abiding, all those dharmas likewise have no place of abiding.
"Just as the nature of space is pure, so too are all phenomena.
At that time, the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas spoke again, saying:
"In what should all Tathāgatas abide?"
"From what are they born?
Vairocana Buddha replied,
"O Great Beings!"
"All Tathāgatas abide in their own body, speech, and mind, and they arise from their own body, speech, and mind.
The Buddhas then asked:
"In what does the mind abide?"
He replied,
“It abides like space.
He asked again:
"In what does space abide?
He replied,
"Space abides nowhere."
At that time, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas gave rise to a sense of rare wonder and spoke these words of praise:
"Excellent! Well spoken is the teaching on the nature of one's own mind, wherein all conditioned phenomena are quiescent."
Having spoken these words, he remained silent. Chapter Sixteen:

The Realization of Enlightenment through the Vajra of the Accomplishment of All Maṇḍalas. This is the most supreme, profound secret within secrets of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas, from the Great Assembly of All Buddhas. At that time, all the Tathāgatas once again gathered like clouds.

Then all the Tathāgatas, by means of the three vajra-activities, exhorted the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, to proclaim the profound and secret Dharma-gate; immediately, they manifested various kinds of rare jewels and exquisite ornaments as offerings to the World-Honored One.
At that time, the World-Honored One, Vairocana-vajra Tathāgata, immediately entered the vajra-samādhi known as the Adornment of the King of Fearless Samādhis of the Great Vajra Maṇḍala.

Its measurement is sixteen cubits, and its form is made square;
the maṇḍala of all Buddhas abides as the vajra-body.

The practitioner, following the ritual, should visualize the Secret Vajra.
Reciting the fundamental great vidyā and performing all acts of offering—
this is the practice of the secret samādhi that is difficult to perform.
This is called the Vajra Maṇḍala of the Body of All Tathāgatas, the Samādhi of the Great Vidyā of All Secrets.
At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi called the Adornment of the Vajra Cloud of All Speech.
Emerging from that concentration, he proclaimed the Vajra Speech Maṇḍala through the three vajra activities:
"Furthermore, I shall now explain the maṇḍala of the activity of speech."
Born from the vajra-mind, it excels all maṇḍalas.
Measuring twenty cubits, with four sides and four corners,
