Recite the mantra of the maṇḍala: "O Vajra-guṇa-rāśi, Vajra-mahādharma-rāja, source of all vidyās.
In the center of that maṇḍala, draw a great wheel.
And all the mudrās should be drawn according to the ritual procedures.
In the center of the great wheel, draw the mudrā of Amitāyus;
this is the vajra phrase that constitutes the supreme maṇḍala.
Acting according to the ritual manual, do not allow for any impairment;
by presenting secret offerings, one attains the joy of the Vajra.
Through that nectar-samādhi, one accomplishes the perfection of offering.
"This is what is called the practice of the difficult-to-perform samādhi of all Buddhas.
"This is named the Vajra-speech Maṇḍala of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Universal Cloud Vajra.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he proclaimed the supreme secret within secrets, the heart maṇḍala, by means of the three vajra-activities:
"One should draw the maṇḍala, and in its center, Vajrapāṇi,
according to the ritual procedures of one's own family, arising from the secret three activities."
"This is called the Heart Maṇḍala Born from the Most Supreme and Profound Secret within Secrets, the Vajra Wisdom Syllables of the Body, Speech, and Mind of all Tathāgatas."
At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi called "The Adornment of the Wheel Producing All Maṇḍalas of All Tathāgatas.

Emerging from that concentration, he proclaimed through the three vajra-actions the teachings on all secret maṇḍalas, as well as the mudrās of all those vajra maṇḍalas, and the teachings on the secrets of the heart-mantras and so forth:
"Now, the vidyā for drawing the lines of the maṇḍala is spoken: [mantra]"

"HŪṂ OṂ ĀŚAHAḤ. (1) When laying out the five-colored powders with the vajra-line, one should recite this great mantra; by performing it according to the ritual procedures and in accordance with the Dharma, one will swiftly attain the Bodhi of all Buddhas."

From that samādhi rite arise the vidyās of the noble ones abiding in the words of empowerment; the supreme rite of the great maṇḍala; the words for the body-maṇḍala arising from the Great Sovereign Vairocana and the Bodhisattva Locanā; and the manifestation of one’s own image arising from the Sovereign of the Vajra Dharma, the Merit of Body-Vajra. This is the most supreme secret among all vidyās, eternally arising from the Great Sovereign Vajrasattva; and from this most supreme secret arise all the vidyās of the Bodhisattva Māmakī.

Thus, when all the requisites for the maṇḍala are fully assembled and one abides in the supreme secret, this is the invocation of the King of Wrath, the most rare and supreme great secret of the Vajra.

"By making offerings to all Buddhas as performed during the three periods of the day, one makes offerings to the non-abiding Three Vajras; by becoming united with those Three Vajras, one attains the Great Illumination (Mahāvidyā) and accomplishes all Great Illuminations."

One should offer the "raw food" (*āmisa*) as a gift to the various *bhūtas*; these five kinds of nectar arise from one’s own mind. Such a samādhi is supreme and peerless, capable of swiftly bringing the Bodhi of all Buddhas to full completion.
"If one wishes to cast the lines to construct a maṇḍala, it should be done in this manner:

while casting the lines, one should visualize Vairocana and the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, as well as the great radiance of the Dharma-vajra such as Vajrāmṛta; one should visualize all the *karmas* (ritual activities) of all Buddhas and contemplate that those vajra-lines are themselves the five Buddhas—this is called the supreme secret and unprecedented [teaching] of all Buddhas."
"It should be known that there are twenty-five kinds of powder used, as explained in the ritual manuals (*vidhi*).
One should visualize all *mahāvidyās* as the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi; thereby, one immediately attains the samādhi of the secret, supreme bodhi-body, speech, and mind of all Buddhas."

When one visualizes these five locations and completes the practice in this manner, one immediately attains the indestructible vajra born of the three vajras. Just as all terrors are dispelled by the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, so too do all nooses, vajra-hooks, and even all the teachings of the Vajra-vidyās arise from the samādhi of the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi’s firm and correct wisdom.

All procedures for performing homa, including their great mantras and even the materials used for the homa, should be performed with the *rahu-śikhā* (the crest of Rāhu), all according to the ritual manuals. When these two aspects are in equal correspondence, perform the homa eight hundred times; one will then attain the three kinds of indestructible vajras. This is called the "Difficult Practice of Samādhi" of the Homa of All Buddhas.
"As previously explained, this is the method for laying the lines of the Great Maṇḍala; the measurements of all the lines are as described in the ritual manual.

Once the lines have been laid, one constructs the Vajradhātu Maṇḍala. Within the maṇḍala, according to the ritual procedures, one places the image of the principal deity Vairocana and the various deities and sages. Furthermore, within the altar, one places five auspicious vases (kalaśas) according to their respective positions."
Having constructed the maṇḍala, the Vajrācārya then receives the disciples according to the ritual procedures.
Once they have been received, he instructs them according to the Dharma, speaking these words:
"You should abide in the three vajra-actions; may Vajrasattva empower your body, speech, and mind."
Thereafter, lead the disciple into the maṇḍala.
At the moment of entering the maṇḍala, recite this great vidyā-mantra:
"Aḥ (1) Khaṃ-vī-ra Hūṃ (2). This is named the Great Vidyā-mantra of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of All Samādhis.

"Once you have entered the maṇḍala, the secret wisdom of the great vajra empowerment shall be conferred. You should visualize all Buddhas filling the realm of space and make offerings with exquisite incense and the like; furthermore, praise them with songs of sublime melody. Visualize clouds of the Great Samaya pervading the great vajra maṇḍala, and abide in the samādhi of the Three Vajras."
Thereafter, the Vajrācārya shall cast white mustard seeds upon the body of the disciple.
Having cast them, he should take the vessel of excellence (*bhadraghaṭa*) and confer the empowerment.
At that time, when the disciple receives the empowerment, he should visualize himself as Vajrasattva.

Having received the empowerment, one abides in the supreme samādhi, constantly dwelling in the firm mind-dharma of Vairocana. All actions performed accord with right wisdom, and one cultivates the vajra activities of body, speech, and mind. One takes refuge in all the worthy sages of the three realms and respectfully practices all the instructions spoken by the ācārya. One practices according to principle all the secret empowerment dharmas; this is the True Dharma born from the three secrets of all Tathāgatas, the great vajra meaning bestowed upon disciples, the various secret bodhi-vajras, and the vast samādhis conferred by all Buddhas.

"At that time, once the disciple has received the empowerment, they should give rise to a state of supreme and great joy. With all the images of the worthy and holy ones abiding in a mind of meditative correspondence, the Ācārya may then point out the method of the Great Maṇḍala and bestow the great vidyā-syllables, secret phrases, and so forth."
Furthermore, he spoke the vow of samādhi, saying these words:
“Those acts of killing, stealing, sexual misconduct, and lying— The intrinsic nature of all such defiled phenomena—
One who abides in the Buddha’s samādhi Should understand them as they truly are.”

"This is called the Supreme Samādhi of All Buddhas, the Dharma of Eternal Abiding, which causes all sentient beings to dwell securely in the vajra-correspondence, and through which one correctly proclaims all mantra-syllables (*vidyā-pada*), all methods of samādhi, the ritual procedures for the Secret Vidyārāja-mantras, and other secret nectar-dharmas."
For any practitioner who acts according to the Dharma, unsurpassed bodhi will not be difficult to attain.

It should be known that these four great secret dharmas of the noble ones are themselves the All-Secret Vajra; manifesting in the form of women, they abide in the Great Wheel Samādhi and perform deeds for the benefit of all sentient beings, proclaiming the secret ritual manuals of the great mantras of all vajra maṇḍalas.
If one consumes those five kinds of food and drink according to the ritual, one will thus attain the accomplishment of all great vidyās.

At that time, having spoken thus, the ācārya further reveals to his disciple the secret conduct of the great maṇḍala and proclaims the vajra secret syllables. He immediately recites the syllable *Oṃ*, which is the root of all great vidyās. In an instant, its light blazes forth, universally illuminating all; this is called the secret great vidyā of the Buddhas, the Great Vidyādharas, and it is also the great samaya of all accomplishments, the supreme practice for the accomplishment of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, and the vajra-syllable of powerful and diligent *antardhāna* (invisibility) and invocation within the maṇḍala of all vajra activities.
Abiding in the visualization of the Vajra of Emptiness, with the radiance of the syllable Hrīḥ,
one further visualizes all Buddhas filling the realm of empty space;
their body, speech, and mind are in union with the great mantra.
"This is the secret mantra of the empowerment of the Vajra of Great Radiance of Body, Speech, and Mind.
As for 'A Khaṃ Khe':
The image of Vajrapāṇi, Padmapāṇi of Great Light."
"Invincible image, abiding in the secret syllable.
This is the Great Vajra Secret Syllable.
In the solar maṇḍala, the Honored One Akṣobhya appears in the center."
Within the great vajra wheel, Vairocana appears;
within that very great wheel, Amitāyus further appears.
These secret minds and all secret meanings—
A great radiance appears, illuminating all who suffer extreme pain.
This is the secret heart-mantra of all vajras:
"The letter A-vajra, as well as the various vajra-hooks."
All those ritual procedures accomplish the awakening of the Buddhas.
Any practitioners who cultivate the Dharma should go to mountain forests, wildernesses,
or other excellent locations, and practice according to the Dharma.
Within half a month, he attained the fulfillment of the Buddha-nature.
Those thirty-six hundred, equal in measure to Mount Sumeru,
as numerous as the atoms of dust in their entirety— all those in the various assemblies— [were transformed].
They all attain it, becoming the Vajra of Bodhi.
This is the Great Laughter Samādhi of the Vajra of all Buddhas.
Vajrapāṇi of great wisdom, holding the Great Speech Vajra.
The Great Sign of the Body-Vajra explains the *kiṃkara* rite:
"This consists of the four great vidyās of the Vajra-Wisdom Wheel—namely, the samaya-phrase, the samaya-speech, the samaya-love, and the samaya-fist."
"Vast and pure as space, transcending all phenomena,
manifesting perfect and wondrous marks— this vajra is unprecedented.
All Buddhas universally observe all sentient beings."
Equal toward all as if toward an only son, they are sustained by all Buddhas.
Beloved by Vajrapāṇi, this vast secret mind causes one to abide in the three vajras as the Great Vajradhara.
Abiding in emptiness, one should visualize the Great Powerful Sublime Vajra,
wearing a sublime jewel crown and joined with the five vāṇas;
he is the Great Vajra Wrathful One, possessing the great vidyās at his five locations.
Whether one is foolish or wise, if they practice visualization according to the Dharma,
within half a month they will attain secret accomplishment—
the great meaning of the secret vajra vajra-song.
Abiding in emptiness, one should visualize the Great Maṇḍala of the Buddha;
with the Vajra-vidyā of the syllable HŪṂ, one visualizes the three vajras and so forth.
Visualizing the syllable OṂ at the eyes, one is able to perceive all things.
And seeing the marks of all Buddhas, the supreme Vajra of the three bodies;
though hunger, thirst, and the like are great sufferings for the world,
the practitioner of yoga does not give rise to thoughts of them.
Far removed from all suffering, one accomplishes the Vajra Mind, the image of the Honored One Vairocana, the correct phrase for all meanings.
The syllable *vaṃ* is the Vajra Mouth; the syllable *oṃ* is the Vajra Eye.
Those two syllables, Oṃ and Vaṃ, abide upon the vajra tongue.
Dwelling nowhere in any place, free from all suffering and tranquil, they are the light of the wisdom-vajra;
they are themselves the wondrous wish-fulfilling jewel.
In accordance with the aspirations of sentient beings, all things are adorned.
This is called the "Vajra Wish-Fulfilling Jewel of All Buddhas.
The *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra*, the Supreme Secret Great King of Teachings on the Three Vajra Actions of All Tathāgatas, Fascicle Five.
The Sixth Fascicle of the *Buddhabhāṣita-sarvatathāgata-vajrakāya-vāk-citta-parama-rahasya-mahātantrarāja*,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.

Translated by the Dharma-transmitting Master, Your Servant Śīlagupta, by Imperial Decree. The Sixteenth Part: The Subsequent Section on the Realization of Bodhi through the Vajra of All Maṇḍala Accomplishments from the Great Assembly of All Buddhas, the Most Supreme, Profound, and Secret of the Secrets of the Three Vajra Activities of All Tathāgatas. At that time, the World-Honored One—the Great Vajradhara, the Great Vajra Fearless One, the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana—entered the vajra samādhi known as the Great Fearless Stainless.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he spoke these words of illumination through his own three karmas:
"Vīṃ. Having spoken this word of illumination, he further recited a verse:
"Visualize the space-vajra, The Buddha-light maṇḍala."
Appearing as a yellow Vajra, Vajravetālī,
with all marks perfectly complete and adorned with every ornament,
wearing the crown of all Buddhas upon her head, she abides in universal equanimity.
"Through the union of the three vajras, all accomplishments are brought forth.
At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi of the Universal Sound Vajra.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he spoke these mantra-syllables regarding the activities of body, speech, and mind through the visualization of the Great Vajra:
"Jum-jum. Having spoken these mantra-syllables, he further recited this verse:
"Visualize the space-vajra, The solar maṇḍala."
Pervading the clouds of all Buddhas, The sovereign of the three vajras,
Within the maṇḍala, one should visualize the Bodhisattva Cundā,
Her body manifesting the appearance of white, Adorned with every ornament.
From the three vajra-karmas, he is born with firm stability;
abiding as Vajrapāṇi, the Great Being, he upholds the vidyā-mantra.
This is called the Samādhi of the Radiant Wisdom of the Vajra Samaya.
At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the samādhi of the Great Bliss of All-Vow Vajra.
Emerging from that concentration, he proclaimed these mantra-syllables with his body, speech, and mind through the Samādhi-Vajra-Equanimity:
“KHAM. Having spoken this mantra-syllable, he further spoke these verses:
Visualize the space-vajra, the vajra maṇḍala;
visualize the vajra-born, all the Tathāgatas.
In the center, visualize the deity Ratnagarbha, manifesting in the form of a great yakṣa.
Wearing a crown of precious topknots, his form and features are serene and tranquil.
Abiding in union with the five Buddhas, he visualizes them at the five locations;
attaining the vajra nectar, he manifests in the posture of meditative sitting.
Furthermore, he is in joyful union with Vajrapāṇi;
such is the Yakṣa Lord, the powerful Treasure God (Ratnagarbha).
This is called the Samādhi of the Auspicious Banner of Great Wealth Accomplishment through the Vajra Samaya.
At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the *vajrakāmeśvarī-śrī-samādhi*.
Emerging from that concentration, he proclaimed these mantra syllables through the bodily, vocal, and mental activities of all the yakṣiṇīs:
“CĀRU. Having spoken these mantra syllables, he further spoke this verse:
"Visualize the vajra of space, a maṇḍala of the four directions adorned with the four jewels, complete with incense, flowers, and all requisites,
filling the entire realm of space, wherein all ḍākinīs appear."
Born from the three vajras, visualize them as a single image;
the indestructible three vajras abide in the visualization of meditative concentration.
Through the samādhi of the sublime vajra, visualize the crown of the wrathful deity.
Abiding in the mantra-syllables of the mind, one practices the conduct corresponding to the vajra.
This is called the Vajra Samādhi of the Visualization of the Equal Conduct of All Ḍākinīs.
At that time, the World-Honored One again entered the Samādhi of the Vajra of the All-Vajra Great Mantra Vidyottama.
Emerging from that concentration, he spoke this Dharma with his own three karmas:
"Body, speech, and mind are pure; one maintains the physical forms and marks of all Buddhas."
Like the light of purple-gold, it accomplishes all siddhis;
the *antardhāna* and other rites, with their equal and wondrous radiance;
the accomplishment of the Yakṣa lords, and the Great Honored One of the Vidyādharīs.
The accomplishments of all vajras, the accomplishments of all exquisite forms,
and the accomplishments of all great mantras appear everywhere.
The accomplishments of all Buddha-uṣṇīṣas are the wondrous light of the wish-fulfilling jewel.
"The supreme Buddha-bodhi, the vajra-light of all Buddhas—
this is called the 'Vajra Samādhi that Perfects All Vows of All Buddhas.

At that time, the Vajradhara— the Great Lord of Secrets of all Tathāgatas, who has accomplished the vajra-vidyā-practices of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas— the Vajratathāgata Mahāvairocana again proclaimed this Dharma with his own three karmas:
The vajras of body, speech, and mind, the nature of body, speech, and mind,
their own characteristics and their own activities— all these are accomplished.
Corresponding with the syllables of Locanā, one visualizes the vajra insignia.
One should skillfully study the characteristics of the great mudrās according to the teachings.
Abiding in the secret of all Tathāgatas and dwelling in the Buddha’s bodhi,
one should perform secret offerings during the four periods of the day.
Flowers, fruits, and all such things—whatever is obtained, one should eat as it comes.
Thus one will swiftly attain the supreme ocean of great wisdom of all Buddhas.
When the six-month period is fulfilled, the ritual practice shall be accomplished.
The hosts of all bhūtas cannot afflict oneself or others.
One should understand the nature of Rāgavajra according to the Dharma;
the great hook of Rāgavajra is the merit of Māmakī.
Visualize the Vajra of Speech; success is attained everywhere.
Through the meditative concentration on the self-seal and the three-syllable vajra—this great wisdom of all Buddhas—the transgressor shall be destroyed.
The Great Sovereign Vajra, born from the vajra syllables,
[subdues] all asuras, nāgas, yakṣiṇīs, and even mānuṣīs,
who abide within the wisdom of the three vajras.
Each should perform the various vidyādhara rites according to the methods of their respective families.
Such great mantras are the secret and true teachings,
born from the three vajras and entering the bodhi of all Buddhas.
"This is called the Samādhi of the True Vajra Vidyādhara of All Tathāgatas.

The seventeenth chapter, titled "The King of the Vajra Empowerment of the Samādhi Dharma of All Tathāgatas," from the *Great Assembly of All Buddhas*, the most supreme and profound secret within secrets of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas. At that time, all the Tathāgatas once again gathered like clouds.
Then all the Tathāgatas, each with their own three karmas, exhorted the World-Honored One, Vairocana-Vajra, to proclaim the secret dharma, speaking these words of praise:
“The vast wisdom of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, The vajra-dharmadhātu,
most wondrous, The samantamukha, the triple firmness— We take refuge in the sound of the secret, sublime Dharma.”
Vairocana Buddha is pure, the supreme Great Bliss, the Vajra of Quiescence;
the self-nature of all phenomena is pure radiance. I take refuge in and pay homage to the one who proclaims the Vajra Dharma.
Ratnasambhava Tathāgata is profoundly sublime, Like the realm of space, free from all defilement;
His self-nature is pure and originally signless— I take refuge in him who excellently teaches all secrets.
Amitāyus Buddha, the Great Sovereign, Abiding as a Vajra, free from all doubt and confusion,
Having realized the self-nature of desire and reached the further shore, I take refuge in that which is proclaimed by the Lotus Family.
Amoghasiddhi Buddha, with perfect wisdom, Is able to fulfill the vows of all sentient beings;
With a nature pure, abiding in the limit of reality, I take refuge in the Vajra Supreme Being.
Thus are praised the words of tranquility, proclaimed by all the Tathāgatas;
if practitioners of the Dharma extol them, they shall become equal to the Buddhas.
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, the compassionate one of all Buddhas, again from the Vajra of Speech, spoke these secret verses:
“Great indeed are all Buddhas! The Dharma-realm is free from letters.”
"Intrinsic nature is fundamentally pure, Like space, free from defilement.
At that time, the Great Lord of Secrets of all Buddhas, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, abiding in the vajra-samādhi of the body of all Tathāgatas, spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind:
"Those four kinds of samādhi arise from the ocean of the Buddha’s wisdom."
"Having attained unimpeded mastery over food and drink, this samādhi is supreme.
Furthermore, abiding in the Samādhi of the Vajra Speech of All Tathāgatas, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mental activity:
"Those four kinds of samādhis are the Great Syllables of Vajra Speech."
"Having realized the five kinds of nectar, this secret is brought forth.
Furthermore, abiding in the samādhi of all Vajradharas, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind activities:
"Those four kinds of samādhis are also the dharma of nectar."
Born from the great power of Vajrasattva,
The vajras of body, speech, and mind, Arising from the Great Samaya,
Abiding in the ultimate state of all Buddhas, And sustained by the Vajra.
"Through the Vajrapāṇi-samādhi and the Great Radiance of Vajrapāṇi,
in a single kṣaṇa, one attains the three activities of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, abiding in the samādhi of all pratyekabuddhas, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind-activity:
“Skillfully teaching the dharmas of the body, that body abides as vajra;
teaching the characteristics of the precepts for sentient beings, it abides in ultimate equality.
Furthermore, dwelling in the samādhi of all śrāvakas’ training, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mental activity:
"These ten paths of wholesome action, produced by the vajra of wisdom,
give rise to these various samādhis, which are termed 'inferior liberations. Furthermore,
abiding in the Samādhi of All Brahmā Kings, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind:
“Delusion is the path of all karmas; it manifests as a form of great terror.
By following the Bodhi of the Buddha, one immediately attains the vajra-body.
Furthermore, abiding in the *rūdradeva-samādhi*, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind:
"Abiding throughout all the three realms, sought by the three vajras, the nature of desire is threefold, arising from the supreme samādhi. Furthermore,
abiding in the samādhi of the deity Viṣṇu, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mental activity:
“Sentient beings abide in the limit of reality; the three vajras are indestructible.
Entering the samādhi-vajra of meditative concentration, they are the space-vajra realm.
Furthermore, abiding in the samādhi of the three vajras, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind activities:
"All those who possess the Body-Vajra are the Great Brahmā;
those who possess the Speech-Vajra are Maheśvara;
and those who possess the Mind-Vajra King are Viṣṇu."
"These three heavens are the abodes of the three vajras.
Furthermore, abiding in the samādhi of all yakṣas and yakṣiṇīs, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind:
"Constantly abide in the dharma of desire; indulge freely in all eating and devouring."
"Without abandoning the three vajras, one performs the samādhi that is most difficult to accomplish.
Furthermore, abiding in the samādhi of all nāga kings, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind:
"The *śuṇḍa* of those who always delight [in it], with *citra* as their food and drink."
"According to whatever fragrant objects are desired,
the samādhi that is produced therein causes all afflictions to follow and turn accordingly.
Furthermore, abiding in the *sarvāsurakanyāsamādhi*, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind:
"Manifesting as a wrathful and fierce one, delighting in flowers and fruits, abiding on the vajra-ground,
he is difficult to tame and most terrifying. Furthermore,
abiding in the *sarva-rākṣasa-siddhi-samādhi*, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, mind, and activity:
“Karpūra, Śekhara, Dāra, and Vāsaka—these are the hosts of bhūtas.
This is called the Great Samādhi;
it is also auspicious and brings about great benefit.”
Furthermore, abiding in the samādhi of all ḍākinīs, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind:
"Those such as Rudhira and the rest are constantly their food and drink;
this is the sign of arising through union with the ḍākinī-samādhi."
"Since self-nature is unproduced and there is no movement within the three realms,
by abiding in the samādhi of non-movement, one attains all accomplishments.
This is called the 'Samādhi of Equality of All Vajra Samādhis of the Three Realms.'"
Furthermore, abiding in the accomplishment of the vajra-samādhi of bodily action, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind:
"The three types of bodily actions Are born from all vajras;
Pervading the realm of sentient beings, They are the constant activity of the Buddha-body."
Furthermore, abiding in the activity of speech, or by means of the Vajra-samādhi, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind-activities:
"The phrases of vocal activity are undefiled; The three realms are pure and perfected.
This is the accomplishment of speech, The practice of the difficult-to-perform samādhi."
Furthermore, abiding in the accomplishment of the mental activity of the Vajra-samādhi, he spoke these words from his own body,
speech, and mind: “The ground of the vajra-intent, The conception of vajra-solidity— As described in the samādhi, The three vajras are indestructible.”
Furthermore, abiding in the Samādhi of the Reality of All Great Vidyās and Vajras, he spoke these words from his own body,
speech, and mental activities: "All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, The assembly of Pratyekabuddhas and Śrāvakas,
Through the correspondence of body, speech, and mind, Attain the supreme accomplishment."
Furthermore, abiding in the vajra-samādhi of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, he spoke these words from the activity of his own body,
speech, and mind: "That Vajrasattva, in every respect, abides as the firm maṇḍala of body, speech, and mind."
"The meditative absorption of the three vajras, In accordance with reality, is conjoined;
Abiding in all the great vidyās, This is the method of true recitation.
Furthermore, abiding in the samādhi of the accomplishment of the Vajra-vidyā, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind:
“The realm of sentient beings is equal; abiding in the vajra-samādhi, the supreme of the three vajras, it is born from the vajra-samādhi.
Furthermore, dwelling in the near-attainment, the supreme attainment, and the great attainment of vajra-samādhi, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mental activity:
"Visualize the Vajra Nectar filling the entire realm of space;
bestowed by the three vajras, it abides eternally in the supreme samādhi.
Furthermore, dwelling in the Samādhi of the Empowerment (Anuttāna) of All Vajras, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind:
"All secret dharmas, practiced at the four times as supreme,
in accordance with that samādhi, are the perfection of vajra. Furthermore,
abiding in the samādhi of the vidyādhara of space, he spoke these words from his own body, speech, and mind:
"The vajras of body, speech, and mind, crowned by meditative concentration—
through the samādhi of the three vajras, one cannot give rise to wrath. Furthermore,
abiding in the karma-samādhi of all those who hold the great vidyās, he spoke these words from his own activities of body, speech, and mind:
"The body-vajra is firm and solid; externally, it is upheld by the vajra.
This is the activity of the dharma-vajra, performed according to the ritual manual.
This is called the Great Vajra Samādhi of the Self-Nature of all Buddhas."

At that time, after the Lord of Great Secrets, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, had spoken these and other dharmas of samādhi, he remained in silence within the inconceivable realm of the equality of the vajra body, speech, and mind activities of all the great Vajradharas.

At that time, in the assembly, there were bodhisattva-mahāsattvas as numerous as the atoms in as many Mount Sumerus as there are in incalculable and innumerable buddha-fields. Having each prostrated themselves at the feet of all the Tathāgatas, they addressed them thus:
"Why does the Great Secret Lord of all Buddhas, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, remain silent within this great assembly of all the Buddhas and bodhisattvas?"
At that time, all the Tathāgatas addressed the Bodhisattvas, saying:
“Sons of good family, you should know this:

the vajra body, speech, and mind are unapprehendable; the self-nature of all syllables and phrases is likewise unapprehendable. All the syllables and phrases of the body, speech, and mind of every Tathāgata are without self-nature and are not even characterized by conditioned activity. For this reason, we remain in silence.”
"O sons of good family!

This mind of the Tathāgata likewise abides in this manner: that body, speech, and mind are free from letters, unarisen, and without marks; like space, they lack substantiality, and all are comprised within the unreal."
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī and the other great bodhisattvas addressed the Tathāgatas, saying: "So it is, so it is."
“World-Honored One!
The intrinsic nature of the dharmadhātu of all Tathāgatas is without activity and without fabrication; it neither comes nor goes.
For this reason, all syllables and phrases produced by Vāgvajra are subsumed within the category of the unreal.”

At that time, there was a great bodhisattva in the assembly named Brahmādyo. Although he had already attained the wisdom of great supernormal powers (*abhijñā*), he had not yet fully understood the self-nature (*svabhāva*) of the characteristics of all phenomena (*dharma*). Having heard this teaching, he asked:
"How is it that the vajra-great-self dharma and other vajra-truth secret syllables are proclaimed?"
At that time, all the Tathāgatas addressed that bodhisattva, saying:
"You should abide in accordance with reality, just as you have realized the Dharma.
The bodhisattva Brahmādyo then spoke again:
“O Buddhas, World-Honored Ones!

Although I have attained the secret syllables of the vajra body, speech, and mind as they truly are, I have not yet fully understood that vajra enlightenment; I pray that all Tathāgatas will reveal it to me.”
The Buddhas replied:
"Son of good family!
Letters have no intrinsic nature; in reality, nothing is produced."
That vajra-bodhi is embraced until the very end of the realm of sentient beings, universally causing all to abide securely in the vajra-bodhi of all Buddhas. Why is this?
"The vajra-wisdom of body, speech, and mind attained by those sentient beings is all produced from the vajra-dharmatā of the three bodies.
At that time, the Great Lord of Secrets of all Buddhas, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Vajrapāṇi, again addressed the Tathāgatas and the Bodhisattvas, saying:

"The dharma-realm is non-abiding; all phenomena are selfless and pure by nature. From within this non-abiding, the ritual procedures for generating all phenomena arise as vajras; though there is practice, it is not [an object of] practice."
Then all the Tathāgatas together praised the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying these words:
"O Great Being!
Regarding all the vajra-achievements of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, as well as all phenomena within the triple world—upon what language do they depend for their abiding?"
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva said:
"The Vajra-accomplishment of all Tathāgatas is the knowledge of all-knowledge; furthermore, all phenomena within the triple world abide in reliance upon the vajra body, speech, and mind."
The Tathāgatas asked:
"Upon what should body, speech, and mind abide?
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva replied:
"It abides like space," said the Tathāgatas.
"In what does space abide?"
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva said:
"Space has no abode; because emptiness has no abode, all phenomena are likewise.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas gave rise to a sense of wonder and spoke these words:
“Magnificent, magnificent!
Vajrasattva has excellently proclaimed this. It is so, it is so;
if body, speech, and mind do not exist, then their formal characteristics (*rūpa-lakṣaṇa*) are likewise unapprehendable.”
At that time, Vajrapāṇi, revered by the three realms,
praised by all Buddhas, the Lord of Vast Secrets,
abiding in the firmness of the three secrets, attained mastery over the three vajras.
The Vidyādhara Mahāsattva proclaimed all accomplishments:
"Abiding in the empty vajra-realm, visualize the Buddha-maṇḍala;
within it, manifest as the Body-Vajra, and contemplate the Vajra-summit."
Born from the three faces and three bodies, through inconceivable transformations,
holding the great vajra wheel, one swiftly attains great enlightenment.
Regarding all the dharmas of the various families, one should visualize this secret.
If one visualizes a separate dharma, that will not bring accomplishment.
This is called the Vidyādhara Mahāsattva’s Vajra Secret Dharma.
"Abiding in the realm of space, visualize the host of bhūta-rākṣasīs."
Generating such joy, one manifests the three vajra signs.
If one meditates in this way, the Bodhisattva will be greatly enamored,
and within seven days, one shall attain the accomplishment of the three bodies.
At that time, the Lord of Great Secrets of all Buddhas, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, further proclaimed the vajra-secret dharma for all practitioners through his own body,
speech, and mind: "Through the three vajras of one's own being, the meaning of the great mudrā of samādhi,
and by visualizing the signs of the various ritual procedures, one attains the realization of buddha-nature."
Furthermore, by means of his own body, speech, and mind activities, he proclaimed the Vajra Secret Dharma for all practitioners:
"Even if one does not form the mudrās, by reciting the various great mantras,
one shall not transgress this samādhi and will attain the accomplishment of awakening."
Furthermore, by means of the activities of his own body, speech, and mind, he proclaimed the secret dharmas of the samādhis of all Buddhas:
"Do not give rise to doubt or slander upon seeing those five kinds of nectar;
these three secrets of the vajra are to be employed according to the dharma."
Furthermore, by means of the activities of his own body, speech, and mind, he proclaimed the secret dharma of the Vajra Speech Samādhi:
"All the *ūṣmānta* syllables that exist within the three realms—
All those secret dharmas are the Vajra Speech, free from censure."
Furthermore, by means of the activities of his own body, speech, and mind, he proclaimed the secret dharma of the Vajra-Samādhi of Mind:
"All samādhis abide in the vajra of the three bodies;
the Samādhi of the Vajra-Bhairava is the non-reproach of the Vajra of Mind."
"This is called the Vajra Samādhi of the Three Mysteries of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, by means of his own body, speech, and mind activities, he proclaimed the Vajra Secret Dharma of all Tathāgatas:
"The five Tathāgatas turn the wheel; The meaning of the five aggregates is equal."
That vajra-abiding dharma is the bodhisattva maṇḍala.
Furthermore, he proclaimed the secret dharma of the samaya-wheel of the three realms through his own body, speech, mind, and activity:
“The earth element is the Honored One Locanā; the water element is Māmakī.”
The Fire Element is the Honored One Vairocana; the Wind Element is Tārā and the rest.
The Space Element is the Vajra Realm, which is none other than Vajrasattva.
One should know that these great elements are themselves the manifestation of all the Bodhisattvas.
"This is called the Samādhi of the Great Vajra-sattva, the Sovereign of the Vast Palace of All Tathāgatas.

At that time, the World-Honored One, abiding in the body, speech, and mind-activities of all Tathāgatas, the Great Vairocana Vajra-Tathāgata entered the samādhi of the Equal Practice of All Tathāgatas.
Having emerged from meditative absorption and having universally observed all the Tathāgatas and their assemblies, he remained silent.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya rose, respectfully prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One Mahāvairocana and all the Tathāgatas, and spoke these words:
"How should one view all the secret congregations of the vajra body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas; the meaning of all empowerments; all Tathāgatas; all Bodhisattvas; and even the Vajrācārya?"
The Buddha said: "Good son!
All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and even Vajrācāryas and the like, all abide in the vajra-bodhicitta; you should view them in this way."
Why is this? That bodhicitta and the ācārya are non-dual, lacking the characteristic of duality.
"O noble son!
I shall now speak briefly.

All the Buddhas, Tathāgatas, and Bodhisattvas throughout the worlds of the ten directions who currently abide, preach the Dharma, and teach sentient beings—all of them come at the three times of day to the presence of the ācārya, where the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas manifest clouds of transformed offerings to make their worship.
Having performed the offerings, they returned to their respective Buddha-fields.
At that time, the Ācārya, emerging from Vāgvajra, also spoke these words:
"All Tathāgatas are my father; all Tathāgatas are my mother; all Tathāgatas are my teacher."
“Maitreya, you should know this:

all the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, as well as the practices of those Buddhas, and even all the accumulations of merit born from the vajra body, speech, and mind of the Tathāgatas—all such accumulations of merit arise from the pores of the ācārya.”
Why is this? Son of good family!
From that bodhicitta arise the true births of the wisdom of all Buddhas, and they abide in truth; even so it is with the characteristics of the knowledge of all modes of knowledge (*sarvajñajñāna*).
At that time, having heard these words, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya was struck with awe and fear, and remained silent.

Then, the World-Honored Ones—Akṣobhya Tathāgata, Ratnasaṃbhava Tathāgata, Amitāyus Tathāgata, and Amoghasiddhi Tathāgata—immediately and simultaneously entered the Vajra-samādhi known as the "Vajra of Diligent Pursuit for the Accomplishment of All Vajradharas."
Having emerged from this, they all spoke these words:
"O Bodhisattvas, you should now listen attentively:

All the Tathāgatas of the ten directions, throughout the three times, have come to this Secret Assembly born of their wisdom to make offerings to the Vajra-Initiation Ācārya, and furthermore, they pay him homage and offer praise."
Why is this? O sons of noble family!
The Vajrācārya is a great wielder of the vajra; he is the sovereign of the great wisdom of all Buddhas.
At that time, those great bodhisattvas addressed these questions to the Tathāgatas:
"Buddhas, World-Honored Ones!
Upon what should the vajra-attainment of all the secret body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas rely?"
The Buddhas replied:
“The three secrets of the Tathāgatas should abide in the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of the Ācārya.
They asked again:
"Furthermore, how do this very body, speech, and mind abide? He replied:
"They are simply non-existent and without attachment."
When the bodhisattvas had heard this teaching, they remained silent.
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, again addressed the Tathāgatas and the bodhisattvas, saying:
"Listen attentively, listen attentively, O Buddhas and bodhisattvas!"
"I shall now proclaim the Dharma of the Great Maṇḍala Born of the Vajra Samādhi of all Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.
At that time, all the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas paid their respects and spoke these words:
"Excellent, O Great Vajradhara!"
Well said, Blessed One! Well said, Sugata!
Great Maṇḍala!
At that time, the World-Honored One, the Tathāgata Vairocana-Vajra, spoke these verses:
"Just as the space of the pure Dharma-realm, Visualize the Buddha-maṇḍala,
With its four directions of pure and wondrous appearance."
The Vajra-maṇḍala, the Aśana-cakra,
and various other offerings— these should be performed constantly according to the ritual;
abiding in the heart of the ācārya is the method of the equal empowerment.
Visualize that within the realm of empty space, all Buddhas are omnipresent;
from their various ritual procedures arise the three types of consecration verses,
through which one attains the accomplishment of Bodhi for the benefit of sentient beings.
The accomplishment of body, speech, and mind is the most excellent among all accomplishments;
it is the heart of all Tathāgatas, which is unsurpassed enlightenment.
This is called the Great Maṇḍala Born of the Samādhi of the Great Wheel Samaya of All Buddhas and Bodhisattvas.

At that time, the Great Lord of Secrets of all Buddhas, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, further proclaimed through his own body, speech, and mind-activity the secret great vidyā-mantra of the three vajra-actions of all Tathāgatas,
which is the vajra-correspondence of the vajras: "One should visualize the realm of space as the secret maṇḍala,
born from the heart of the three secrets."
Visualize Vajrasattva manifesting in a form of great wrath, with the color of a blue lotus.
According to the ritual, visualize him with four arms,
holding a kapāla and radiating five kinds of light.
Furthermore, visualize one’s own tongue as being in union with the Vajra-samādhi; it summons the Dharma-words of nectar.
Through the trident, the vajra, the vajra-hook, and so forth, which are in union with the vajra, one accomplishes the bodies of all Buddhas.
Furthermore, by means of the activities of body, speech, and mind, he proclaimed the Vajra Food and Drink Samādhi rite:
"If one partakes of food and drink, etc., In accordance with the ritual,
it accords with nectar (amṛta) And does not transgress any of the ritual procedures."
Furthermore, by means of the activities of his own body, speech, and mind, he proclaimed the supreme method of worship through the three activities of all Tathāgatas:
“The fivefold methods of worship constitute the most excellent offering;
this is the universal vajra, the practice of the difficult-to-perform samādhi.”
Furthermore, by means of the activities of one’s own body, speech, and mind, he proclaimed the secret method of offering through the three activities:
“By uniting with the two places, one should partake of that nectar;
by making offerings according to the ritual procedure, one attains the awakening of Buddhahood.”
Furthermore, by means of the activities of his own body, speech, and mind, he proclaimed the ritual methods for the three activities of all Tathāgatas:
“The realm of sentient beings is boundless; Pervasive and held with universal equality, Through the samādhi of the three vajras, One causes them to abide in the Great Marvel.”
Furthermore, by means of his own body, speech, and mind, he proclaimed the supreme methods of the three types of action for all practitioners:
"Through mastery over body, speech, and mind, The three secrets arise without abiding;
All that is sought shall be accomplished, But for those who transgress, there is no success."
Furthermore, by means of his own body, speech, and mind activities, he proclaimed the supreme dharma of Vajrasattva for all practitioners:
"One should fashion a crown maṇḍala measuring one cubit,
in which the syllable Oṃ appears, produced from the five nectars."
Through union with the Supreme Vajra, light manifests in an instant;
with body, speech, and mind well-established, all that is undertaken is accomplished.
Furthermore, through the activities of his own body, speech, and mind, he proclaimed the secret methods of the threefold activity for all vidyādharas:
“May all vidyādhara practitioners remain far removed from all signs of existence;
without giving rise to a mind of grasping or attachment, they should construct stūpas, temples, and the like.”
"Do not recite the scriptures; do not construct maṇḍalas.
If one is in accord with the intrinsic nature, this is the supreme [practice].
Furthermore, he proclaimed through the activities of his own body, speech, and mind the secret methods for neutralizing all poisons, subjugating, and summoning:
"Abiding within the great wheel, one should visualize white flames blazing and pervading everywhere, as well as yellow light and so forth.
These are the three vajras, the great radiance of samādhi."
"Born from the seeds of those three secrets.
Furthermore, with his own body, speech, and mind, he proclaimed the *vidyā* for the protection of the vajra-unified activity of the wheels of body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, saying:
"This *vidyā* abides as the Vajra Karma-cakra."
Within the wheel appears the syllable HŪṂ, and within that, one writes its name.
The great vidyā-syllables and the correct phrases abide eternally according to the rite;
this is the totality of all vidyās, the non-abiding of the three secrets.
Furthermore, by means of his own body, speech, and mind activities, he proclaimed the Vajrāñjana rite:
"The practitioner should go to a crossroads,
or beneath a tree, or even to a temple and such places, and perform the añjana rite."
One should take a kapāla, place the rudhira and other substances within it,
and on the fourteenth day of the dark fortnight, during the middle of the night,
recite the vidyā-mantra of one’s own family eight hundred times while performing the empowerment.
"Attaining the threefold accomplishment, as well as the *añjana* rite—
this is called the secret practice of Samantabhadra by all Buddhas.
At that time, all Tathāgatas addressed the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, saying:

"How do the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas come to be fully endowed with all secret syllables and phrases, so that they are able to develop firm faith and understanding in all the secret samādhi practices of the Tathāgatas and contemplate them according to reality?"
At that time, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva said:
“O Buddhas, World-Honored Ones!

If bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain mastery over these three kinds of secret syllables and phrases, they will be able to develop firm faith and understanding in the secret samādhi-practices of all Tathāgatas and perform meditative visualizations according to reality.”
The Tathāgatas asked,
"What are these three?
Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva replied:
That is to say:
the vajra body of all Tathāgatas, the vajra speech of all Tathāgatas, and the vajra mind of all Tathāgatas; these are called the three secret syllables and phrases.

If one can thus attain such perfection, those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas will then be able to cultivate firm faith and understanding in the samādhi-practices of all Tathāgatas, and contemplate them according to reality.
At that time, after all the Buddhas had each praised the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, they remained silent.
Then, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi addressed all those Tathāgatas and Bodhisattvas, saying:
"Great Beings, you should know:

This Dharma is profoundly deep, secret, and rare. Since the appearance in the world of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Dīpaṃkara, until the appearance in the world of the Tathāgata Kāśyapa—throughout all these kalpas, as numerous as the atoms of dust that cannot be compared or calculated—not a single one of these Buddhas has ever proclaimed this secret Dharma.
Why is this? Because at that time, sentient beings lacked faith and understanding, and were thus unable to comprehend the meaning of these secret phrases of merit.

For this reason, during that period, all the Buddhas and Tathāgatas did not proclaim the supreme Mahāyāna Secret Assembly, the Dharma of the Bodhi of all Buddhas; even for a kṣaṇa, a lava, a muhūrta, or a moment, they could not hear this secret Dharma for even an instant.

Even if one were to exert oneself with diligent and arduous effort throughout countless *gaṅgā*-sands of eons, one would still be unable to attain the Buddha’s bodhi, because one has not been able to hear this great secret Dharma.
"Therefore, all Buddhas should know:
this secret Dharma is extremely difficult to encounter.
At that time, having heard these words, the great Bodhisattvas in the assembly immediately wept with tears of sorrow.
Then all the Tathāgatas said to those bodhisattvas:
"Stop, sons of good family!
You should not weep or wail in sorrow, nor give rise to thoughts of the three kinds of suffering."
At that time, the bodhisattvas addressed the buddhas, saying:
“Buddhas, World-Honored Ones!
How can we now cease our weeping?”
How can one not give rise to the three kinds of suffering and affliction?
I contemplate that sentient beings are obstructed by ignorance; they do not give rise to faith or understanding regarding the three secret phrases, and have not even heard their names.
The Tathāgatas said:
"O sons of good family!

The syllables and phrases as they are attained are entirely equal; they are not something that can be known by knowing, nor something that can be heard by hearing. All Tathāgatas and all Bodhisattvas find nothing at all within those secret syllables and phrases, and they have no realization of them whatsoever."
"Why is this? Because the self-nature of the syllables and phrases of the three secrets is intrinsically pure.
At that time, having heard these words, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas remained silent.
The Sixth Fascicle of the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra*, the King of the Most Secret Great Teachings on the Three Vajra Activities of All Tathāgatas;
The Seventh Fascicle of the *Sarvatathāgatatattvasaṃgraha-nāma-mahāyāna-sūtra*, the King of the Most Secret Great Teachings on the Three Vajra Activities of All Tathāgatas.

Translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Court-Attendant of the Third Rank, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, and Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, under Imperial Edict.

The Remainder of the Seventeenth Chapter: The King of Vajra Empowerment through the Samādhi-Dharmas of All Tathāgatas, from the *Great Assembly of All Buddhas: The Most Supreme and Profound Secret within Secrets of the Three Vajra-Karmas of All Tathāgatas*. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Locanā, having emerged from the secrets of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, joyfully praised the Lord of the Great Secrets of all Tathāgatas, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, with her own three karmas amidst the great assembly, speaking these words:
“O Vajrapāṇi, Great Sovereign, Well-established in the supreme Vajra-mind, ... [text continues] ...”
In accordance with all desires and all that is sought, you rescue and deliver the entire realm of sentient beings.
You are the true Dharma, the very nature of desire and bliss, the supreme Vajra, and the Great Beloved.
Therefore, I take refuge in you and offer praise; I pray only that you will accept me according to the Dharma.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Māmakī, having emerged from the secrets of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas, joyfully praised the Great Secret Lord of all Tathāgatas, Vajrapāṇi Bodhisattva, in the midst of the great assembly, saying these words:
“O Vajrapāṇi, you who benefit sentient beings, You who are well-established in the great wheel of the adamantine mind;
From the supreme mind of the Buddha’s bodhi, You have brought forth the first principle of the vajra.”
The nature of all desire and desire itself are equal; my own intent accords with this truth.
Therefore, I take refuge and offer praise once more: may you, in accordance with the Dharma, graciously accept me.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Avalokiteśvara, amidst the great assembly, joyfully praised the Lord of the Great Secrets of all Buddhas, the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, speaking these words:
“O Vajrapāṇi, you who possess great compassion, Through vajra speech, you bring vast benefit and happiness;
In accordance with the various aims and benefits of the world, You constantly proclaim the affairs of the world.”
All that exists of the nature of bliss is entirely subsumed within the true practice of Samantabhadra;
therefore, I take refuge and offer praise once more, praying only that you may accept me according to the Dharma.

At that time, all the Tathāgatas, arising from the equality of the vajra body, speech, and mind activities, with minds of supreme joy and delight, praised the Bodhisattva Vajrapāṇi, the Great Lord of Secrets of all Buddhas,
speaking these words: “O Vajrapāṇi of great benefit and bliss, Abiding in the supreme secret samādhi,
You give rise to the hearts of reverence and love for all Buddhas, And extend impartial compassion to all beings.”
The treasury of all great desires and merits, Complete with every supreme and rare treasure—
Therefore, I rejoice and offer praise, Accepting you according to your wishes.
At that time, the Great Lord of Secrets of all Buddhas, the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana, entered the samādhi known as the Auspicious Vajra of Sovereignty over the Nature of All Great Desire.
Having emerged from meditative absorption, he remained silently within the samādhi of the self-nature of the great desire for the correct practice arising from all Tathāgatas.
At that time, all Tathāgatas who filled the realm of space each abided in the supreme, most profound, secret-of-secrets Vajra-nectar Great Samādhi-practice through their three vajra-actions.

At that time, signs appeared in the sky, whereby all sentient beings throughout the entire realm of space became established in the vajra-glorious nature of phenomena born from the equality of the three bodies;

they immediately attained the three vajra wisdoms of all Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and all came to abide in the pure dharma-realm of Samantabhadra, receiving the vajra empowerment of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas.
At that time, the Great Secret Lord of all Buddhas, Vairocana Vajra Tathāgata, addressed the Tathāgatas, saying:
"Do the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, now perceive this sign and abide in the equality of the nature of all Buddha-dharmas?"
The Buddhas replied:
“We have seen them,
World-Honored One!”
"I have seen them, Sugata!
All these such signs are the vajra-wisdom practices of all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas."
At that time, all the Buddhas, having fully established themselves in the secret practice of the foremost vidyā-queen of all Tathāgatas, spoke these words of praise:
"How marvelous!"
World-Honored One!
How rare! Sugata!
"This is what is called the syllables and phrases of non-attachment that lead skillfully to the path of the Buddha's Bodhi.
At that time, Vairocana Vajra Tathāgata addressed the Buddhas, saying:
"Buddhas, you should know:"

The intrinsic nature of the space-vajra samādhi is equal; all those phenomena are not the aggregate of form, not the aggregate of feeling, not the aggregate of perception, not the aggregate of formations, and not the aggregate of consciousness. They are not the sense bases, not the elements, and not the characteristics of grasping. They are not desire, hatred, or delusion; they are neither dharma nor non-dharma. One should abide in this manner.
When all the Tathāgatas had heard these words, they remained silent.
Then, the Vajra Tathāgata Mahāvairocana again addressed the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, saying:

"All Bodhisattvas in all worlds should, with sincere faith and sincere acceptance, practice according to the principle this most supreme, profound, and secret True Dharma of the three vajra-actions of all Tathāgatas."
"Why is this? Because this Dharma is extremely profound and exceedingly difficult to attain.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the Bodhisattva Vajradharma within the assembly, saying:
“Good son! You have already attained mastery over all dharmas and have received the vajra empowerment from all Buddhas; you should now uphold this secret dharma.”
Then, having received the Buddha’s command, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Vajradharma remained silent.

At that time, all the Tathāgatas again entered from their own body, speech, and mind-vajras into the samādhi of the syllables and correct phrases of those three vajra-mahāsattvas, and there they abided.

Furthermore, the World-Honored One, the Vajra Tathāgata of the Body of Mahāvairocana, remained silent within the equality of the bodies of all Tathāgatas, amidst the secret activities of the three karmas of all body-vajras throughout the triple world.

Furthermore, the World-Honored One, Vajratathāgata of Immeasurable Life Speech, remained silent within the equality of the speech of all Tathāgatas and the vajra-conduct of all speech in the three realms.

Furthermore, the World-Honored One, Akṣobhya-citta-vajra Tathāgata, remained silent within the equality of the minds of all Tathāgatas, which is the vajra-conduct of the mind of all within the triple world.

Chapter Eighteen: The Bestowal of the Vajra Empowerment for Proclaiming All Secret Practices. From the Great Assembly of All Buddhas, the Most Supreme and Profound Secret within Secrets of the Vajra Body, Speech, and Mind of All Tathāgatas. At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Maitreya, being within the great assembly, beheld all the Tathāgatas proclaiming the secret dharma-gates of the empowerment of the body, speech, and mind of all Tathāgatas. Having heard and seen them exactly as they were spoken and according to those samādhis, he spoke these words:

“Magnificent! The most supreme and profound body, speech, and mind activities of Samantabhadra’s pure dharmadhātu; the threefold secret and victorious conduct of the vajras; the vast and universal dharma of the mind-vajra; that which gives birth to all sentient beings as the self-nature of the three-time vajras; the attainment of great bodhi, the vajra correct phrase, and the vast power of the vajras of all Buddhas.”
How great is this profound and wondrous, supreme wisdom!
How great is this tranquility, the root of all phenomena!
How great is this supreme realm of Great Nirvāṇa!
"How magnificent is the cessation of all paths of saṃsāra!
At that time, having heard these words of praise from the Bodhisattva Maitreya, all the Tathāgatas addressed him, saying:
"Maitreya!..."
"It is as you have said; it is so, it is so.

At that time, the assembly of great Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas gathered once more like clouds. Having each made the most supreme secret offerings to all the Tathāgatas, they all paid homage with reverence and prostrated themselves, speaking these words with one voice:
"How marvelous! This profound and wondrous teaching, so difficult to hear, such a secret form of practice within this Great Assembly, is the most honored and supreme among all dharmas."

The speech of all Buddhas, the Great Guides, abides in accordance with reality as firm and great wisdom; for the benefit of sentient beings, we now have some questions to ask. We pray that the Buddha, out of compassion, will explain them for us.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas praised them, saying:
"Excellent, excellent,
O Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas!"

If one realizes that sinful phenomena are not truly sinful, and likewise regarding the fruits of merit;
if one realizes that both sin and merit are non-existent, such a person shall proceed toward the practice of enlightenment.
Not relying on those verbal expressions, one immediately attains that which is entirely indestructible;
no evil destinies shall arise for such a person, and that great bodhi will not be difficult to attain.
The causal karmic offenses previously committed by them are called the "hell" of these evil fruits;
yet whether that hell arises or does not arise, this fruit of hell is ultimately unattainable.
All the countless seals of phenomena (*dharmamudrā*) abide securely in the great vajra of bodhi;
through supreme realization free from grasping, they dwell in resonance with infinite sentient beings.
Free from grasping and non-grasping regarding all karma, those various activities are not under the control of a sovereign;
that which is correctly performed achieves great accomplishment, for all ritual actions are equal.
At that time, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having heard the Buddhas proclaim the profound, true Dharma born of the great compassion of all vajras, were filled with joy and offered this praise:
“Excellent, excellent, O Honored One of the World!”
Excellent, excellent, Great Muni!
Excellent, excellent, Great Sublime Dharma!
Excellent, excellent, Great Compassionate One!
How great is the compassionate conduct of Samantabhadra!
Supreme, vast, pure, and stainless, He performs the rites of wrathful *karma*, Causing all sentient beings to enter the Buddha-nature.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas again addressed the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, saying:
"O sons of noble family!

Upon hearing this Dharma of the Great Assembly for the Secret Empowerment of All Tathāgatas, you must not give rise to fear or alarm, nor should you harbor contempt or slander toward it; rather, you should abide in samāpatti."

Why is this? Because the Bodhi-vajra arises from the limit of reality (bhūtakoṭi), because the nature of Dveṣa-vajra is vast, and because it is embraced by the Great Illumination (mahāvidyā) that is free from bondage.
At that time, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, with one voice and in unison, again praised all the Tathāgatas, speaking these words:
“Born from the vajra-reality-limit (*bhūtakoṭi*) of the three times, Tranquil, free from obstructions, and pure—
To the supreme Great Sovereign of all Buddhas, The Vajra of the three supreme activities, we pay homage.”
All form, sensation, perception, mental formations, and consciousness, The six sense faculties and the six sense objects are all like illusions;
Earth, water, fire, wind, and space— I take refuge in that which is manifested from the bodhicitta.
Those defiled phenomena of greed, hatred, and delusion, Constantly practiced in accordance with the Vajra Dharma, All various aspects abide within the true nature;
I take refuge in the Bodhicitta that manifests extensively.
If one grasps at the marks of all pleasant phenomena, those phenomena are by their very nature unmoving;
the nature of cause and effect is born of the mind, and the nature of all phenomena is devoid of mental marks.
The faults of greed and other afflictions, as well as all obstacles, All abide within the vajra that is unborn;
And that bodhicitta is vast— I take refuge in that which manifests all phenomena.
This abiding is pure, without beginning, and so forth;
born from the dharmas of wisdom and skillful means, it is eternally conjoined with the secret empowerment—to the Bodhicitta-vajra, I perpetually pay homage.
If one contemplates these dharmas as supreme, the practitioner will certainly fulfill the meaning of each of the three types of accomplishment; I perpetually take refuge in Bodhivajra.
If one performs the rite of Vajra-accomplishment, one should abandon all inferior accomplishments;
honoring the Buddhas and generating pure faith, one should perpetually take refuge in Bodhicitta-vajra.
Now, this teaching of the Secret Assembly is rare even for those who merely hear it;
how much more so for those who read, recite, contemplate it, honor, make offerings to, or transcribe it?
The merit gained from this is inexhaustible; I perpetually take refuge in Bodhivajra.

Regarding the various ritual manuals for pacifying and other rites, as well as the great mantras, mudrās, and their applications— whatever is performed according to principle shall be accomplished; I perpetually take refuge in Bodhivajra.
Now, regarding this most supreme secret dharma, if there are those who see, hear, or rejoice in it,
and can give rise to even a single thought of pure faith, the merit they obtain will be boundless;
how much more so for the practitioner who, relying on this dharma, cultivates the corresponding secret conduct?
"This mass of merit has been extensively proclaimed; I perpetually take refuge in the Bodhi-Vajra.
At that time, having heard these praises offered by the bodhisattvas, all the Tathāgatas expressed their sympathetic joy and said in praise:
"Excellent! Excellent!"
The assembly of bodhisattvas has eloquently spoken these words; they are the sovereigns among all phenomena, most honored and supreme, born from the secret assembly of the Tathāgatas.

Having spoken these words, all the Tathāgatas and the assembly of Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas each dwelt securely in the three karmas of firmness, and all entered into the sameness of the nature of the Vajra body, speech, and mind, remaining in silence.
At that time, the Tathāgata Body-Vajra, having again established himself in the dharma of the equality of body, remained in silence within the equality of the bodies of all Tathāgatas.

Furthermore, the Vajra Speech Tathāgata, having likewise established himself within all verbal activities of the triple world, remained silent in the state of equality of the speech of all those Tathāgatas.

Furthermore, the Tathāgata Citta-vajra, having likewise established himself within all mental phenomena of the triple world, remained silent within the equanimity of the minds of all those Tathāgatas.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the entire great assembly, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all filled with joy, and they received it with faith, practiced it, and put it into effect.
